policydecision_details: The Republic of Moldova has approved a 2027 fiscal package designed to generate €254.7 million (USD 292 million) in state revenue through tax restructuring and excise hikes. The reform adjusts personal income tax exemptions, modifies VAT thresholds for various sectors including hospitality and agriculture, and increases excise duties on fuel and tobacco. Additionally, it introduces new VAT charges for cross-border e-commerce consignments under €150. The policy aims to shift the fiscal burden from production and labor toward consumption and negative externalities while providing corporate investment incentives.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government seeks to rebalance the fiscal burden to stimulate investment and simplify administrative compliance. By taxing 'vices' and consumption more heavily, the administration aims to generate necessary budget revenue while maintaining stable income tax baselines for households and businesses.
decision_making_institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova
additionalcommodities: Vegetables and derived products|Fruits and derived products

policydecision_details: The government of Curaçao has announced an investment of XCG 3 million to build an integrated digital healthcare system. This initiative, scheduled to run from 2027 to 2029, aims to strengthen cybersecurity and protect patients' medical information. The project will develop new policies for data protection and establish a secure infrastructure for information exchange between healthcare providers. Additionally, the government intends to create a legal and organizational framework to support population health management and improve public-health surveillance.
contextoradditionalinfo: Curaçao's current healthcare information system is fragmented, with data distributed across various institutions, which hinders efficient patient care and limits the use of health data for policy decision-making. Furthermore, the lack of a uniform cybersecurity framework has increased the risk of data leaks and cyberattacks on critical healthcare systems. This investment is part of a broader effort to modernize the healthcare sector and transition toward data-driven health policy.

policydecision_details: Prime Minister James Marape has announced a new policy to provide long-term concessional loans to farmers of coffee, cocoa, and copra. Starting next year, funding will be made available through the National Banking Corporation (NBC) to support agricultural development along major highway corridors. The loans will feature a repayment rate of four to six percent over a 40-year period. This initiative is designed to stimulate economic growth and help the nation reach a K200 billion economy threshold.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of the broader 'Connect PNG' programme, which focuses on improving road connectivity to unlock economic opportunities in rural areas. The government aims to leverage improved infrastructure to increase agricultural exports and support the livelihoods of one million families. This effort is aligned with the government's long-term vision to build national unity and economic prosperity.
beneficiaries: coffee farmers, cocoa farmers, copra farmers, small to medium enterprise activities

policydecision_details: The Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress has approved a new Law on Farmland Protection and Quality Improvement and a revised Agriculture Law. These laws establish a legal framework for designating permanent basic farmland, implementing a compensation system for occupied farmland, and setting quality standards for high-standard farmland projects. The revised Agriculture Law focuses on protecting farmers' rights, increasing their incomes, and reducing the administrative burden on rural areas. Both laws are set to take effect on January 1, 2027, to strengthen food security and modernize agricultural production systems. The legislation also mandates that agriculture remains a priority for government fiscal support.
contextoradditionalinfo: The legislation was introduced to address the need for standardized, law-based protection of arable land and to improve governance efficiency in the agricultural sector. By creating a legal negative list for land designation and ensuring that any occupied farmland is replaced with equivalent quality and quantity, the government aims to secure the core of the country's food security. Additionally, the revision of the Agriculture Law seeks to address issues like formalism at the grassroots level and to better integrate household farming with modern agricultural practices.
decision_making_institution: Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress

policydecision_details: The government of Uzbekistan has announced a reduction in the unified customs duty rate for goods imported by individuals for personal use, dropping from 30% to 20% of the customs value. Additionally, the minimum fee for these imports will be lowered from US$3 to US$2 per kilogram. Starting 1 June 2027, the policy will further waive standard customs processing fees if the calculated unified customs payment is lower than those fees. These changes amend the previous Presidential Resolution No. PP-4508 of 7 November 2019. The measure is part of the broader 'New Customs of Uzbekistan — 2030' strategy to simplify procedures and increase automation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of the 'New Customs of Uzbekistan — 2030' strategy, which aims to modernize and simplify customs operations, reduce clearance times, and increase the automation of customs processes to 60% by 2030. It specifically targets non-commercial imports by individuals to facilitate personal travel and cross-border movement of goods.

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: The German Cabinet of Ministers has approved amendments to the Energy Industry Act to reduce the annual federal subsidy for electricity grid charges. The subsidy will be lowered from the current €6.5 billion in 2026 (USD 7.5 billion) to €5.52 billion (USD 6.4 billion) annually for the period between 2027 and 2029. This funding is provided through the German Climate and Transformation Fund and is intended to be factored into network tariff calculations for transmission system operators. The decision aims to adjust the fiscal support provided to industrial enterprises for grid usage costs.
contextoradditionalinfo: The subsidy was originally introduced in January 2026 to support approximately 600,000 industrial enterprises by lowering electricity grid usage charges. The government is now adjusting this support as part of a broader strategy that includes the abolition of the gas storage levy and reductions in electricity taxes. The decision has faced criticism from industry associations, particularly the German Steel Association, which argues that the reduction threatens planning security and the competitiveness of energy-intensive businesses amid geopolitical uncertainty.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Chinese Premier Li Qiang signed a decree promulgating 19-article regulations to strengthen the management of local market regulatory authorities. These regulations aim to streamline regulatory mechanisms, optimize staffing, and improve administrative services for market entities. Key duties include registering self-employed individuals, conducting routine oversight of food production and sales, and handling market complaints. The policy emphasizes minimizing disruption to business operations while ensuring transparency and fair competition.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of China's broader effort to build a unified national market and foster a favorable business environment. It aligns with the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), which prioritizes improving market regulatory rules, unifying standards, and enhancing regulatory capabilities to ensure high-quality market order and healthy competition.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: Uzbekistan has introduced a presidential decree to expand support for entrepreneurs and families through the creation of sustainable jobs. The policy provides unsecured loans of up to 5 billion soums to entrepreneurs who cooperate with families listed in the Social Register. Additionally, a mechanism to compensate interest expenses on commercial bank loans for small and medium-sized businesses will be implemented starting 1 October 2026. The decree also reforms social support by introducing a multidimensional assessment system for social assistance and providing childcare benefits for working women. District and city headquarters are empowered to manage these credit resources and social assistance funds to ensure targeted and efficient implementation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy aims to increase household incomes and accelerate the development of small businesses by creating sustainable jobs and providing financial support to vulnerable families and entrepreneurs. It addresses socioeconomic challenges by integrating financial support with a new points-based social assessment system.
beneficiaries: entrepreneurs, families in the Social Register, self-employed people, small and medium-sized businesses, women

policydecision_details: The Chinese State Council has issued a decree to revise the Regulations on Management of Housing Provident Fund, effective September 20, 2026. The reform expands the scope of fund usage, allowing withdrawals for home renovations and property management fees, while removing income-based eligibility thresholds for rent payments. It also broadens investment channels for the funds to include policy-oriented financial bonds and simplifies application procedures. Furthermore, the policy extends coverage to include individual business owners and flexible workers, while strengthening credit record management.
contextoradditionalinfo: The revision aims to enhance the efficiency and utility of the housing provident fund system, providing greater financial flexibility for contributors and expanding the system's reach to include workers in the flexible employment sector.
beneficiaries: employees, individual business owners, part-time employees, flexible employment workers

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Finance of Ukraine and the World Bank signed a loan agreement for the Tenth Additional Financing of the PEACE in Ukraine project. Under this agreement, Ukraine will receive USD 841 million backed by a guarantee from the Government of Canada. The funds are designated to provide budget support by reimbursing state expenditures for old-age social payments. This initiative is part of a broader effort to maintain the resilience of public finances and ensure the funding of critical social obligations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The financing is part of the ongoing PEACE in Ukraine project, which serves as a critical instrument for supporting the state budget during the conflict. The project aims to mobilize resources to cover essential social expenditures and maintain financial stability. Additionally, the government is working on the SPUR 2.0 initiative to further mobilize international financial support for recovery needs.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Republic of Moldova has updated its flood risk management plans for the 2026–2031 period. The initiative focuses on restoring and maintaining critical hydraulic infrastructure, including dams, drainage systems, and reservoirs. It also mandates the establishment of new automated meteorological and hydrological stations to improve early-warning capabilities. Furthermore, the plan includes specific measures to protect settlements near small rivers through reforestation and the preservation of floodplain vegetation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is designed to mitigate the long-term risks associated with flooding, which threatens settlements and agricultural areas near small rivers. By modernizing monitoring systems and restoring natural riparian buffers, the government aims to enhance climate resilience and protect infrastructure from hydrological hazards.
decision_making_institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Republic of Moldova has launched a €45 million regional water infrastructure project to connect the capital, Chisinau, with the central districts of Straseni and Calarasi. The project involves the construction of a new water intake facility on the Dniester River, two automated pumping stations, and extensive connecting pipelines. This utility network is designed to provide modernized drinking water access to approximately 820,000 residents. The initiative is supported by a €14 million (USD 16 million) grant from the German government and is being implemented under the Open Urban Development Program.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is part of a strategic effort to modernize national utility infrastructure and improve access to essential services for the population in central Moldova. It is facilitated through an inter-institutional cooperation agreement aimed at enhancing regional development and infrastructure capacity.
beneficiaries: residents of central Moldova, residents of Chisinau, residents of Straseni, residents of Calarasi

policydecision_details: The Republic of Moldova has adopted new regulations for municipal sanitation services, covering waste collection, street cleaning, and related environmental maintenance. Local authorities are granted the flexibility to tailor these services based on settlement size, population, and existing infrastructure. The policy mandates a gradual expansion of separate waste collection systems, to be fully implemented by 1 July 2028. Additionally, the regulation establishes clear protocols for the collection of bulky waste and construction debris, while ensuring that service charges are based on actual costs.
contextoradditionalinfo: The regulation aims to modernize municipal waste management infrastructure and improve environmental hygiene across the country. By standardizing waste categories and collection methods, the government seeks to enhance the efficiency of sanitation services and promote better waste sorting practices.
decision_making_institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Republic of Moldova has introduced a new regulatory framework to align its biofuel, bioliquid, and biomass fuel standards with European Union requirements. This regulation establishes clear rules for sustainability certification and supply chain traceability, allowing operators to use EU-recognized schemes without additional local validation. By implementing these standards, the government aims to facilitate market access for Moldovan products and attract investment into the renewable energy sector. The policy also mandates strict compliance with greenhouse gas emission reduction criteria to ensure environmental benefits.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to support the Republic of Moldova’s energy and decarbonization targets, specifically aiming to increase the share of renewable energy to 27 percent of gross final energy consumption by 2030. It also addresses the National Energy and Climate Plan target of achieving 6.9 percent renewable energy in the transport sector by 2030. The regulation serves to harmonize local practices with EU Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/996 and related directives to ensure climate benefits and environmental protection.
beneficiaries: biofuel producers, biomass fuel suppliers, economic operators
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Government of Ukraine has introduced a measure to adjust payment deadlines for export contracts of specific agricultural products. Exporters can now request an extension of up to 180 days for these deadlines. This decision aims to provide producers and exporters with more flexibility to fulfill their contracts. It is intended to help maintain export volumes and ensure continued foreign currency inflows into the country. The measure is designed to support the agricultural sector in securing resources for future sowing seasons.
contextoradditionalinfo: Ongoing military attacks by Russia on civilian vessels and port infrastructure in the Black Sea region have severely disrupted logistics for Ukrainian agricultural exports. These attacks have forced exporters to reroute shipments, leading to significantly increased delivery times and logistical complications that threaten the ability of producers to meet existing contract obligations.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine has approved three legislative measures to implement the Ukraine Plan under the Ukraine Facility. These laws focus on reforming state aid, regulating public service obligations in the state sector, and aligning renewable energy legislation with EU standards. The measures aim to improve transparency in state-owned enterprises and streamline permitting for renewable energy investors. Successful implementation of these laws will unlock EUR 411 million (USD 471 million) in financial assistance from the European Union to support the state budget. This legislative package is a critical step in fulfilling Ukraine's commitments for long-term economic recovery and European integration.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Ukraine Facility is a financial support program running from 2024 to 2027, designed to promote macroeconomic stability, modernization, and reconstruction in Ukraine. Funding is contingent upon the country meeting specific structural indicators outlined in the Ukraine Plan. These legislative reforms are required to meet these indicators and ensure continued financial support from the EU.
beneficiaries: state-owned enterprises, renewable energy investors, industrial park operators
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: The Curaçao Parliament has adopted a motion calling for an independent and in-depth evaluation of the management, capacity, and performance of 2Bays. The government, acting as the majority shareholder, is tasked with commissioning this review to assess the company's progress on strategic objectives. These objectives include promoting energy transition, developing a circular economy, and supporting sustainable industrial development. If the assessment reveals leadership deficiencies, the government is expected to take necessary measures to ensure project goals are met. This initiative aims to address concerns regarding delays in industrial and energy-related projects.
contextoradditionalinfo: Parliamentary concerns have grown regarding the slow pace at which 2Bays is achieving its strategic objectives, particularly those related to the former refinery and industrial areas. There is a broader political debate regarding the future of refinery installations, potential new operators, and the overall financial and operational health of 2Bays and Refineria di Kòrsou. The motion reflects a desire for stronger strategic leadership to ensure that projects vital to the island's economic growth and energy future are effectively implemented.
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: The MAN-PIN parliamentary faction has proposed a new regulatory system to categorize Curaçao’s beaches into five distinct types based on their primary function. This system aims to protect natural heritage, regulate commercial activities, and ensure public access to the coastline. The proposal mandates clear division of responsibilities among three ministries to oversee environmental protection, urban planning, and commercial concessions. It seeks to balance tourism and entrepreneurship with the rights of residents to access and enjoy public coastal areas.
contextoradditionalinfo: The proposal was developed following an evaluation of the current situation at beaches, where the faction identified that commercial installations like beach chairs and umbrellas often occupy significant portions of the coastline. This commercialization, combined with private land ownership surrounding some beaches, has created barriers for residents. The faction argues that current approaches risk excessive commercialization and insufficient consideration for environmental protection and public accessibility.
beneficiaries: residents of Curaçao, local entrepreneurs, tourists

policydecision_details: The National Office of Electricity and Drinking Water (ONEE) has launched a MAD 205.94 million (USD 22 million) infrastructure project to secure the drinking water supply for the cities of Fez and Meknes. The project involves replacing 9.42 kilometers of aging pipeline connected to the Idriss I Dam with a more resilient coated steel pipeline. This initiative aims to enhance the reliability of the regional water transmission system and mitigate risks associated with leaks and ground instability. Public bids for the contract are scheduled to open on September 15, 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: The existing prestressed concrete and steel pipeline infrastructure has suffered from repeated leaks and is poorly suited to the challenging geological conditions of the region, including erosion-prone marl soils, underground cavities, and gypsum pockets. Additionally, heavy traffic along the national road has placed significant stress on the aging pipeline, necessitating a more durable and flexible solution to ensure a consistent water supply for the two cities.
decision_making_institution: National Office of Electricity and Drinking Water (ONEE)
beneficiaries: urban population of Fez, urban population of Meknes

policydecision_details: Prime Minister James Marape has urged customary landowners in Milne Bay to retain ownership of their land rather than selling it to outsiders. The government encourages landowners to register their land under Incorporated Land Groups to secure their rights. The National Government plans to collaborate with the National Development Bank to provide financial access to these groups. This initiative aims to support tourism-related investments and small business development on customary land. The policy emphasizes long-term economic benefits for families and clans through sustainable land use.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is driven by the need to protect customary land as a primary economic asset for local communities in Milne Bay. By preventing the permanent sale of land, the government aims to foster local entrepreneurship in the tourism sector. The upgrade of Gurney Airport serves as a catalyst for this economic development strategy. The government seeks to ensure that tourism revenue remains within the local community to support sustainable livelihoods.
decision_making_institution: Department of Prime Minister and National Executive Council

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Prime Minister James Marape has reaffirmed Papua New Guinea's commitment to climate change mitigation by advocating for stronger global financing through the Green Climate Fund (GCF). The government is leveraging its verified success in reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation to secure results-based payments. These funds are earmarked for reinvestment into forest governance, sustainable land use, and the improvement of livelihoods for forest-dependent communities. Furthermore, the government is actively seeking to expand its ocean conservation efforts, aiming to protect up to 50 percent of its marine areas to serve as carbon sinks.
contextoradditionalinfo: Papua New Guinea holds one of the world's largest tropical rainforest systems and vast ocean territories, which provide critical global environmental services by absorbing carbon. Despite these contributions, the country faces significant climate change impacts, necessitating a shift in the international narrative to recognize Pacific nations as 'big ocean states' rather than just vulnerable small island states. The government is pushing for a more transparent and accountable global system to value these environmental services and channel climate finance effectively to support both conservation and local economic development.
decision_making_institution: Department of Prime Minister and National Executive Council
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Prime Minister James Marape reaffirmed the enduring bilateral partnership between Papua New Guinea and China. The leaders discussed strengthening trade and investment, specifically focusing on the export of liquefied natural gas. The government expressed a desire to move beyond basic government-to-government engagement toward deeper cooperation in downstream processing and energy. This commitment aims to generate practical economic growth and employment opportunities for the people of Papua New Guinea.
contextoradditionalinfo: The reaffirmation occurred during a bilateral meeting on the margins of the 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders’ Meeting. The discussion serves to solidify diplomatic ties and economic cooperation ahead of the upcoming APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. It reflects PNG's strategy to maintain friendly relations with all nations while prioritizing national interests and economic development.
decision_making_institution: Department of Prime Minister and National Executive Council
beneficiaries: our people through, pacific island countries, china, the forthcoming apec, the next time

policydecision_details: The Government of Papua New Guinea has signed a three-year, K26 million contract with TechnologyOne to upgrade the Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS). This initiative aims to modernize public financial management by integrating cloud technology and Artificial Intelligence across all government levels, including national departments, provinces, and districts. The project is designed to enhance transparency, accountability, and the efficient management of public wealth. It serves as a foundational digital reform to support the objectives of the Medium Term Development Plan IV (MTDP IV).
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of Papua New Guinea's administrative journey during its 51st Jubilee year, focusing on digital transformation to improve governance. It addresses the need for a unified public finance ecosystem to ensure that public resources are tracked in real-time and effectively reach intended services. The move is aligned with Strategic Priority Areas 7 and 8 of the MTDP IV, which prioritize national revenue, public finance management, and digital government governance.
decision_making_institution: Department of Prime Minister and National Executive Council
beneficiaries: public finance servants, provincial finance officers, district treasurers

policydecision_details: Uzbekistan and Georgia have established a Working Group on Agricultural Issues to foster bilateral cooperation. The initiative focuses on exchanging expertise in livestock farming, fruit growing, and vegetable production. Both nations aim to integrate scientific research with practical agricultural applications to modernize production methods. Additionally, the partnership explores the introduction of new crops, such as olives, into the Uzbek agricultural landscape.
contextoradditionalinfo: The collaboration stems from a need to modernize the agricultural sector in Uzbekistan by leveraging Georgia's experience with advanced agrotechnologies. By strengthening ties between research institutions and producers, the countries seek to implement joint projects that enhance productivity and diversify crop cultivation.

policydecision_details: The President of Uzbekistan signed a law to improve social services for victims of harassment and violence. The law grants the National Agency for Social Protection authority to manage services for victims and their minor children. It provides exemptions from state fees for essential documents like ID cards and birth certificates for victims in rehabilitation centers. Additionally, it enables 'Inson' social service centers to certify powers of attorney and expands access to state-funded legal assistance for various civil and family law cases. The legislation also allows for the placement of victims in special centers for up to six months.
contextoradditionalinfo: Uzbekistan has been working to strengthen the institutional and legal framework for protecting women's rights and interests. Previous efforts included establishing the National Agency for Social Protection as the primary body for victim support. The new law addresses the need to clarify the agency's powers and formalize the types of social services and legal protections available to victims of harassment and violence.
decision_making_institution: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
beneficiaries: women affected by harassment and violence, minor children of victims

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The President of Uzbekistan signed a law to improve the e-commerce sector by strengthening requirements for electronic trading platform operators. The law amends the Tax Code to establish taxation rules for foreign legal entities providing electronic services or selling goods to individuals in Uzbekistan. It introduces new definitions for order aggregators and digital streaming services while setting clear rights and obligations for operators. Furthermore, the law mandates that sellers bear primary responsibility for contract fulfillment and disputes, with e-commerce operators holding subsidiary liability.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to modernize the country's e-commerce sector, ensure fair taxation of foreign digital service providers, and enhance consumer protection in online transactions. It addresses the need for a clear regulatory framework for cross-border e-commerce and digital product distribution.
decision_making_institution: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
beneficiaries: e-commerce platform operators, foreign legal entities, sellers, self-employed individuals
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has approved a comprehensive strategy for foreign exchange operations and interventions covering the period 2026–2030. The strategy establishes clear objectives, principles, and communication approaches for the regulator's participation in the domestic currency market. It defines the mechanisms for foreign exchange operations, including the sale of proceeds from precious metals and client servicing, as well as interventions to smooth exchange rate volatility. The policy emphasizes maintaining an adequate level of liquid international reserves while supporting an inflation-targeting regime with a floating exchange rate.
contextoradditionalinfo: The strategy was developed in accordance with the laws 'On the Central Bank of the Republic of Uzbekistan' and 'On Currency Regulation' to ensure orderly market functioning and macroeconomic stability. It aims to adapt to structural economic changes, such as the level of dollarization and capital flow liberalization, over the next five years. By formalizing these operations, the Central Bank seeks to enhance transparency and predictability in its market interventions.
beneficiaries: managing international reserves, regime with a, foreign exchange operations, both state and, 2026, reserve management, reconstruction and development, regime or the, foreign currency in

policydecision_details: The government of Uzbekistan has announced a strategic target to achieve 100% water-saving coverage on all cultivated land. This initiative aims to modernize agricultural practices across the country to address water scarcity. The policy focuses on the widespread adoption of water-efficient irrigation technologies. It represents a long-term commitment to sustainable resource management in the agricultural sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: Uzbekistan faces significant water management challenges due to its arid climate and reliance on irrigation for agricultural production. The policy is part of a broader effort to ensure the long-term viability of the country's cultivated land by reducing water waste.

policydecision_details: Uzbekistan has imported 204 head of high-productivity breeding cattle from Russia to the Rishtan district in the Ferghana region. The initiative is designed to enhance local livestock production and improve breeding practices. Specialists from the Ferghana Regional Department of Food Safety conducted inspections to ensure the health and proper housing of the imported animals. The project aims to increase the total number of highly productive cattle in the region to strengthen the agricultural sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The import is part of a broader national strategy to develop the livestock sector, improve breeding potential, and increase productivity within Uzbekistan's agricultural economy.

policydecision_details: President announced a comprehensive socio-economic development plan for Tashkent, focusing on district-specific specialization and infrastructure modernization. The plan includes increasing investment targets to $10 billion for the next year and creating up to 200,000 high-income jobs. Significant funding has been allocated for the renovation of 400 mahallas and 100 streets to improve urban living conditions. Additionally, the government will implement a new system to resolve investor issues directly and increase the limit on unsecured loans for small businesses to 200 million soums. The initiative also covers vocational training, educational infrastructure expansion, and the introduction of intelligent transport systems to manage traffic congestion.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced during a video conference to address the need for utilizing district-specific potential in Tashkent under challenging economic conditions. The government aims to boost added value, attract foreign investment, and improve the quality of life for residents through targeted urban redevelopment and business support programs.
beneficiaries: entrepreneurs, investors, students, residents of Tashkent

policydecision_details: The Lithuanian government has unveiled an €800 million (USD 918 million) 'family package' designed to enhance family security and encourage child-rearing. Key measures include a €110 million child care and activity allowance, increased pension guarantees for parents, and higher sickness benefits for those caring for sick children. The package also proposes universal free school meals for students in grades five through 10, to be implemented between 2029 and 2034. Additionally, it provides financial incentives for families returning to Lithuania from abroad and support for first-time homebuyers.
contextoradditionalinfo: The package is intended to give families a greater sense of security while encouraging people to raise children and remain in Lithuania, addressing concerns regarding poverty, inequality, and emigration.
beneficiaries: families, children, emigrants returning to Lithuania

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The law introduces amendments to Article 14 of the Law 'On the Protection of Consumers’ Rights' to strengthen quality control of goods. It establishes a legal basis for additional quality checks when defects are not identifiable by appearance alone. The policy defines procedures and timeframes for these checks, including the consumer's right to participate or conduct independent checks. It also clarifies the rules for reimbursing expenses related to these quality assessments.
contextoradditionalinfo: In recent years, Uzbekistan has implemented large-scale reforms aimed at protecting consumers’ rights through the development of competition. This specific legislative amendment addresses gaps in the existing legal framework regarding the identification of product defects caused by storage, usage, or third-party actions.
decision_making_institution: Senate of the Republic of Uzbekistan
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
commodity1: Other products, not included in the other categories

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Government of Moldova approved a comprehensive plan for the 2026–2027 heating season, comprising 52 specific measures to ensure energy supply security. The plan focuses on diversifying energy sources, strengthening electricity transmission infrastructure, and mandating natural gas reserves for suppliers. It also includes provisions for energy efficiency in public institutions and residential sectors, alongside technical inspections of energy infrastructure. The initiative aims to mitigate risks from regional instability, volatile market prices, and potential supply disruptions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The plan was developed in response to a challenging regional energy environment, characterized by the ongoing war in Ukraine, volatile international gas prices, and the impact of severe drought on regional electricity generation. These factors have created significant uncertainty regarding energy supply continuity, necessitating proactive government intervention to protect households and the economy.
decision_making_institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The government of Uzbekistan has introduced a new mechanism to manage state property by including non-agricultural land plots that have remained unsold for over three months into the authorized capital of legal entities. To reduce bureaucratic hurdles, these lands are now offered as 'ready-made packages' that include all necessary architectural and construction permits. The state share formed in these enterprises can be bought out by the legal entity through an extraordinary procedure. This policy aims to bring vacant land into economic circulation and accelerate the development of production capacities. The initiative also simplifies the transfer of rights for privatized properties by eliminating the need to re-issue existing lease agreements.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address the issue of long-vacant state-owned land plots that were failing to attract buyers at auction. By removing bureaucratic obstacles and providing pre-approved construction permits, the government seeks to stimulate investment, create jobs, and improve the overall business environment in both urban and remote regions.

policydecision_details: The Hungarian government is launching the Szent István Rural Development Programme to provide targeted financial support to rural communities. The programme allows groups of ten settlements to collaboratively identify their own development priorities, such as infrastructure, medical facilities, and workplaces. A pilot phase involving 100 settlements is currently underway to test the model. Following the pilot, the government plans to implement the programme nationwide, potentially covering 2,174 settlements. The initiative aims to decentralize decision-making and address long-standing economic disparities between rural and urban areas.
contextoradditionalinfo: The programme was introduced to address the decline of rural areas characterized by youth migration, the closure of essential services like schools and shops, and deteriorating infrastructure. Prime Minister Péter Magyar highlighted that rural residents have historically been treated as political constituencies rather than partners. The initiative seeks to bridge the divide between rural and urban Hungary by empowering local communities to manage their own development funds and foster economic sustainability.
budget: 1 billion forint per group of ten settlements annually

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: The Committee of the Brazilian Chamber of Foreign Trade (GECEX) has decided to extend existing anti-dumping duties on imports of seamless carbon steel pipes from Ukraine for an additional five years. The decision follows a sunset review initiated in September 2025, which concluded that removing the measures would likely lead to a resumption of dumped imports and cause injury to the domestic industry. The duty rates remain unchanged from the previous period. This measure is intended to protect the sole domestic producer of these products in Brazil.
contextoradditionalinfo: Brazil first imposed anti-dumping duties on Ukrainian seamless pipes in November 2014, with previous extensions in 2020. The investigation found that the measures were effective, as import volumes from Ukraine fell by 78.3% while the duties were in force. The decision was prompted by a request from Vallourec Soluções Tubulares do Brasil S.A. and concerns regarding the significant export capacity of Ukrainian companies.
decision_making_institution: Committee of the Brazilian Chamber of Foreign Trade (GECEX)
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: Uzbekistan and Serbia have established a joint working group to foster bilateral cooperation in the agricultural sector. The initiative focuses on investment projects, trade expansion, and the transfer of modern technologies, including artificial intelligence and scientific research. Key areas of collaboration include livestock farming, meat processing, fruit production, and seed development. The partnership also aims to improve water resource management and irrigation efficiency in Uzbekistan through Serbian expertise. This framework is designed to facilitate joint production and potential entry into third-country markets.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreement was reached during ministerial talks in Belgrade ahead of an official state visit by the President of Uzbekistan. Both nations seek to leverage their respective strengths—Serbia's research and genetic resources and Uzbekistan's large market and production potential—to address challenges such as climate change and the need for technological modernization in agriculture.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture of Uzbekistan and Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management of Serbia
beneficiaries: agricultural producers, research institutes, agribusiness companies
commodity3: Others meat or animal derived products

policydecision_details: The government of Uzbekistan and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) are in discussions to finance the 'Climate-Resilient Water Supply and Sanitation Systems Development' project. This initiative aims to develop and improve water supply and sanitation infrastructure in the Andijan and Ferghana regions, as well as the Republic of Karakalpakstan. The project is designed to enhance climate resilience in these areas by upgrading essential utility services. The parties are currently exchanging proposals and ideas to finalize the scope and implementation framework of this joint initiative.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is part of a broader effort by Uzbekistan to cooperate with international financial institutions like the ADB to address climate change impacts on critical infrastructure. Improving water supply and sanitation is a priority for the government to ensure sustainable development and public health in regions vulnerable to climate-related water stress.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Economy and Finance of Uzbekistan
beneficiaries: residents of Andijan region, residents of Ferghana region, residents of the Republic of Karakalpakstan

country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
policydecision_details: The UK government has announced a ban on all imports originating from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories. This measure is presented as part of the UK's commitment to a two-state solution. The decision follows criticism of the Israeli government's policies regarding settler-led actions in the West Bank. The ban aims to address concerns over the forced displacement of Palestinians.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is a response to the ongoing situation in the occupied West Bank, where the UK government has accused Israeli officials of encouraging the forced displacement of Palestinians and turning a blind eye to settler-led actions described as ethnic cleansing.

policydecision_details: The Government of Canada is imposing counter-tariffs on USD 27.6 billion worth of imports from the United States effective September 8, 2026. These measures apply tariffs of 15, 25, and 50 percent on specific products. The policy targets sectors including steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics. Administration of these countermeasures is managed by the Canada Border Services Agency. The food measures are concentrated on: Dairy ingredients (mostly 50 percent tariffs), Cheese products (mostly 25 percent tariffs), Honey (50 percent), Molasses (50 percent), Some food preparations and bakery mixes (50 percent).
contextoradditionalinfo: This policy is a retaliatory measure in response to the United States' decision to impose a 50 per cent tariff on $27.6 billion of Canadian goods effective August 22, 2026. Canada aims to protect its domestic industries by matching the U.S. tariffs on a dollar-for-dollar basis.
beneficiaries: domestic producers in steel, dairy, and agricultural sectors

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The Supreme People’s Court of China issued the 'Opinions on the Trial of Cases Involving Artificial Intelligence Disputes', providing the first national judicial guidance for AI-related civil and criminal litigation. The rules establish liability frameworks for AI-generated content, intellectual property, and personality rights, including protections against unauthorized AI face-swapping and voice cloning. It also addresses product liability for autonomous vehicles and sets standards for data protection and algorithmic competition. The policy serves as a regulatory bridge in the absence of dedicated national AI legislation, guiding lower courts on applying existing laws to emerging digital disputes.
contextoradditionalinfo: China has experienced a rapid rise in AI-related legal disputes, necessitating clear judicial guidance to balance technological innovation with security and individual rights. As the country lacks comprehensive AI-specific legislation, the Supreme People’s Court developed these rules to ensure consistent adjudication across lower courts. The guidance aims to support the development of 'new productive forces' while addressing ethical challenges and potential harms, such as algorithmic discrimination and infringement of personal data.
decision_making_institution: Supreme People’s Court of the People’s Republic of China
beneficiaries: AI technology enterprises, software developers, digital content creators
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources inaugurated a modern olive press in the Wilayat of Jabal Akhdar to support local farmers. The facility, costing RO40,000, has a processing capacity of 1.2 tonnes of olives per hour. It is designed to improve crop utilization and enhance the quality of locally produced olive oil. The project serves approximately 500 farmers and is part of a broader plan to expand olive production and marketing in Oman.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project was established in response to the rapid growth of olive cultivation in Jabal Akhdar and the increasing demand for modern processing facilities. With 20,000 trees planted across 80 acres, the sector produces 600 tonnes of olives annually, making the investment critical for supporting the local economy and enhancing food security.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: The Lebanese Cabinet has approved an agreement to import liquefied natural gas via Jordan. The gas will be regasified at the Aqaba facility and transported through Syria to Lebanon to support power generation. This initiative is part of a broader regional energy cooperation effort involving Jordan, Syria, and Lebanon. The project aims to stabilize Lebanon's electricity grid and address chronic energy shortages.
contextoradditionalinfo: Lebanon has been facing severe energy shortages and electricity grid instability for years. Regional electricity interconnection efforts, which were suspended in 2012, have been revived to secure stable energy supplies. The agreement is supported by technical preparations and the rehabilitation of gas transmission networks across the involved countries.

policydecision_details: The US President has signed an executive order to remove endangered species protection for the grey wolf and a subspecies, the Mexican wolf.

policy_description: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements
policydecision_details: Lithuanian Agriculture Minister has ordered the implementation of stricter controls on Russian grain shipments passing through the port of Klaipėda. The new measures require laboratory testing of cargo samples to verify the origin of the grain. These samples are being sent to a laboratory in France for analysis, a process expected to take two to three weeks. This initiative marks the first time Lithuanian authorities have conducted such origin-verification analyses for grain imports.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced following concerns that Russia might be using ports in Latvia and Lithuania to export grain originating from Russian-occupied territories in Ukraine. Ukrainian representatives met with Lithuanian officials to warn about these potential activities. While the handling of Russian grain is not currently subject to international sanctions, the Lithuanian government is taking these steps to ensure the integrity of the supply chain and prevent the transit of goods from occupied regions.
policycategory: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements

policydecision_details: Moldovan lawmakers passed legislation to introduce temporary import licensing for grain and oilseeds. The measure is effective through October 31, 2026. This decision aims to balance the protection of domestic grain growers with the operational needs of the milling and livestock sectors. The government rejected a proposal to extend these restrictions until 2027 to avoid supply bottlenecks and potential food price inflation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to shield domestic agricultural producers from market volatility while addressing concerns from livestock and milling associations regarding supply shortages. Previous interventions of this nature were linked to increases in retail meat prices, prompting the government to adopt a cautious, short-term approach. The decision was debated in parliament, with opposition members questioning the speed of the legislative process and the exclusion of industry lobbies from the licensing commission.
decision_making_institution: Parliament of the Republic of Moldova
beneficiaries: grain growers, livestock producers, milling sector

policydecision_details: The Moldovan parliament approved a bill in the first reading to overhaul agricultural cooperation by replacing informal producer groups with EU-aligned producer organisations. The legislation establishes a legal framework for producer organisations, associations, and interbranch organisations to modernize supply chain cooperation. It introduces operational funds co-financed by member contributions and the National Fund for Agriculture and Rural Development. Additionally, the bill provides state start-up assistance capped at €104,000 per year for newly established organizations. The measure aims to boost competitiveness and prepare domestic agribusinesses for the Common Agricultural Policy.
contextoradditionalinfo: The reform was deemed necessary due to low participation rates under the existing framework and the need to align Moldova's agricultural sector with EU standards and the Common Agricultural Policy. The government seeks to strengthen cooperation among farmers, food processors, and distributors to improve the competitiveness of the agri-food sector and facilitate European integration.
decision_making_institution: Parliament of the Republic of Moldova

policydecision_details: China is expanding its national health insurance coverage to include more innovative drugs for cancer, chronic diseases, rare diseases, and childhood illnesses. The government plans to broaden the scope of innovative medicines covered by commercial health insurance. It will encourage commercial insurers to provide coverage for drugs not currently in the basic program that offer significant clinical benefits. Additionally, the administration aims to shorten approval timelines to accelerate the clinical use of new pharmaceutical innovations.
contextoradditionalinfo: Since 2018, China has added 949 medicines to its national health insurance drug list to ease the financial burden on patients. The country's innovative pharmaceutical sector has grown rapidly, with China accounting for approximately 30 percent of the global biopharma pipeline by 2025. In the first half of 2026, the value of China's innovative drug out-licensing deals reached a record high of over 100 billion U.S. dollars, prompting further integration of these drugs into insurance frameworks.
beneficiaries: patients with cancer, patients with chronic diseases, patients with rare diseases, children with illnesses

policydecision_details: The Chinese government has published the 2026 Development Plan for National Food Safety Standards. This plan outlines the strategic framework and priorities for updating and establishing new food safety regulations throughout the year. It aims to enhance the regulatory environment governing food quality and safety across the country. The initiative reflects a commitment to strengthening national standards to protect public health.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy serves as a roadmap for the continuous improvement of food safety standards in China, ensuring that regulatory frameworks keep pace with evolving food production and safety requirements.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The French government has announced a €1 billion (USD 1.2 billion) emergency aid package to support farmers following a summer of severe drought, heatwaves, and wildfires. The funding aims to compensate for significant crop and livestock losses to prevent farm bankruptcies and maintain national productive capacity. The package includes direct compensation for climate-related losses, tax relief for the most affected farms, and a €235 million fund for feed, seed, and reconstruction. This measure is intended to protect agricultural sovereignty and ensure the continuity of food production in the face of extreme weather events.
contextoradditionalinfo: France experienced an unprecedented summer characterized by extreme heatwaves, wildfires, and drought, which caused yield losses of up to 50% for general crops and as high as 80% for fruits and vegetables. The livestock sector was particularly impacted by shortages of fodder and animal losses. The government introduced this package to address the resulting financial crisis for an estimated 30,000 to 35,000 farms while operating under difficult budgetary conditions.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Lithuania has officially opened the Baltic region's first centre dedicated to cell therapy and personalised medicine in Vilnius. This 3,500-square-metre facility, developed by Northway Biotech, focuses on the development and manufacturing of advanced cell therapies, therapeutic vaccines, and regenerative medicine products. The project represents a 61-million-euro investment aimed at bolstering the country's life sciences sector. It is expected to create approximately 100 highly skilled jobs and contribute to the national goal of increasing the life sciences sector's share of GDP to 5% by 2030.
contextoradditionalinfo: The investment is part of the broader 'Bio City' life sciences ecosystem in Vilnius, which already includes biotechnology manufacturing and gene therapy facilities. The Lithuanian government is actively seeking to leverage its human capital and existing expertise in biotechnology to enhance national competitiveness and economic growth. This initiative aligns with long-term strategic goals to transition the economy toward high-value, innovation-driven sectors.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The Department of Treasury has launched a nationwide public consultation on the Draft Competition and Consumer Protection Bill 2026. This proposed legislation aims to consolidate existing competition and consumer protection provisions into a modern, unified framework. The initiative seeks to promote fair and efficient competition, strengthen consumer rights, and improve regulatory certainty to support economic growth. Public workshops are scheduled across four regions in September 2026 to gather feedback from various stakeholders before finalizing the Bill.
contextoradditionalinfo: The current legislative landscape for competition and consumer protection in Papua New Guinea is fragmented. The government is seeking to modernize these provisions to better support private sector investment, ensure fair market practices, and protect consumer interests through a dedicated and comprehensive legal framework.
beneficiaries: businesses, SMEs, consumers, government agencies, industry associations, professional bodies, civil society organisations
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: The Government of Papua New Guinea has announced a supplementary budget featuring 'belt-tightening' measures to address economic challenges. The policy includes the continuation of fuel subsidies to prevent further price hikes and the removal of GST on 13 essential household items to relieve financial pressure on citizens. Additionally, the government is reallocating funds to support the Electoral Commission for the 2027 General Election and the law and justice sector. These measures aim to stabilize the economy and protect the population from the impacts of the current fuel crisis and El Nino.
contextoradditionalinfo: Papua New Guinea is facing significant economic strain due to rising prices, a fuel crisis, and the adverse impacts of the El Nino weather phenomenon. The government is implementing these fiscal adjustments to manage the national budget effectively for the remainder of the year and to mitigate the cost-of-living crisis for its citizens.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: The revised Agriculture Law of China codifies existing national priorities regarding food security and agricultural development. It serves as a legal framework to reinforce long-standing strategies for maintaining agricultural stability. The legislation integrates current policy goals into a formal structure to ensure consistent implementation across the sector. This revision reflects the government's ongoing commitment to securing domestic food supplies.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy update is part of China's broader effort to strengthen its legal framework for food security and agricultural self-sufficiency. By codifying existing priorities, the government aims to provide a stable regulatory environment for the agricultural sector. This move aligns with national objectives to mitigate risks to food supply chains and ensure long-term agricultural productivity.

policydecision_details: The government of Kuwait has issued a decree that permits the state to borrow funds from its sovereign wealth fund. This measure effectively ends a long-standing ban on such borrowing practices. The decision is intended to provide necessary liquidity to the state treasury. This move is designed to stabilize public finances amidst current economic pressures.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to declining oil revenues and ongoing disruptions to shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz, which have negatively impacted the country's public finances.

policydecision_details: The Bolivian government has ordered an official intervention of the state oil company, Yacimientos Petrolíferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB), to address persistent fuel shortages. The measure involves auditing and reorganizing the import and distribution chain to regularize fuel quotas for service stations. The government also plans a long-term structural shift to transfer YPFB's marketing and retail roles to the private sector. This intervention is intended to last up to 180 days, with a potential 90-day extension, to resolve structural failures and corruption within the supply chain.
contextoradditionalinfo: Bolivia is currently facing a severe national crisis characterized by persistent shortages of diesel and gasoline, with the country importing approximately 60% of its gasoline and 95% of its diesel. These shortages have been exacerbated by smuggling and institutional instability within the state oil company. Recent government attempts to curb smuggling by doubling the price of diesel to $1.50 per liter have triggered widespread protests and roadblocks by farming and transportation groups.
beneficiaries: service stations, transportation groups, farming groups

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The government of Bolivia is facilitating diesel sales and promoting the use of Flex Fuel vehicles. This initiative focuses on the integration of biodiesel and renewable diesel (HVO) into the national fuel supply. The policy aims to modernize the transport sector's energy consumption. It reflects a strategic shift toward alternative fuel sources for the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader regional effort in Latin America to transition toward renewable energy sources in the transport sector. By promoting Flex Fuel vehicles and renewable diesel, Bolivia seeks to reduce reliance on traditional fossil fuels. This move is intended to enhance energy efficiency and support sustainable industrial development.
beneficiaries: more information, advertising and analytics, advertising
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Mexico and Paraguay have officially opened a new trade route for meat products, marked by the first shipment of 22 tons of Mexican pork to Paraguay. This milestone follows the successful fulfillment of stringent sanitary and biosecurity requirements by the Mexican exporter, Altosano Granjas Carroll. Simultaneously, both nations are engaged in ongoing sanitary negotiations to facilitate the export of Paraguayan beef to Mexico by early 2027. The process involves rigorous inspections of slaughterhouses and veterinary systems to ensure equivalence in food safety standards. This expansion of trade aims to diversify market access for producers in both countries.
contextoradditionalinfo: Mexico faces a significant gap between domestic pork production and consumption, making it the world's largest pork importer. Paraguay, a foot-and-mouth disease-free country with vaccination, is seeking to expand its beef export footprint, including potential access to the Mexican market. The trade development is part of a broader strategy to strengthen commercial ties and address domestic demand for animal protein in Mexico.

policydecision_details: The Beninese government has authorized the construction of 35 integrated economic, social, and digital centers across 26 municipalities. These centers will function as social protection one-stop shops (GUPS) to modernize service delivery and improve access for vulnerable populations. The initiative is part of the Productive Social Safety Net Program, which provides financial support to households in extreme poverty. The centers will also integrate digital points and postal services to facilitate economic empowerment and recovery. This project aims to consolidate social protection mechanisms and improve the overall well-being of the most vulnerable citizens.
contextoradditionalinfo: Benin has been actively strengthening its social protection systems to combat extreme poverty, with the poverty rate declining from 33.2% in 2023 to 31% in 2024. The government launched the Gbessoké program in 2023 as a primary instrument for poverty reduction, targeting 150,000 households. The current expansion of infrastructure is a continuation of this broader strategy to modernize social services and provide a safety net against covariant shocks.
beneficiaries: households in extreme poverty, vulnerable households

policydecision_details: The Beninese government has authorized the pilot phase of the Agricultural Productivity and Social Protection Program for farmers, specifically targeting 2,000 corn producers. This integrated program provides agricultural inputs, mechanization services, and technical advice to boost productivity. It also secures producer income through a national aggregation and regulation mechanism. Furthermore, it introduces a social protection component offering health insurance for households and a retirement or term deposit scheme. The pilot will cover approximately 3,000 hectares during the short rainy season of 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government aims to sustainably strengthen the income and social protection of farmers in Benin. By combining productivity support with social safety nets, the program seeks to help farmers better exploit productivity gains and ensure long-term economic security for rural households.

policydecision_details: The South African government has increased the dollar-based reference price (DBRP) for sugar imports from $680 per tonne to $785 per tonne. This adjustment serves as a benchmark to trigger variable tariffs when world sugar prices fall below the reference level. The measure aims to protect local producers from a surge in subsidized foreign sugar imports that have displaced domestic production. Industry stakeholders have welcomed the move but expressed concerns that the increase may not be sufficient to fully mitigate the competitive disadvantage faced by local growers.
contextoradditionalinfo: The South African sugar industry has faced a significant crisis over the past four years, characterized by a sharp rise in duty-paid sugar imports and a 35% decline in local sugar sales. Between 2022 and 2026, import volumes increased more than seventy-fold, leading to substantial revenue losses for growers and millers. The government's decision follows extensive consultations and the consideration of conflicting applications from industry associations regarding the appropriate level of the DBRP.
decision_making_institution: International Trade Administration Commission of South Africa
beneficiaries: sugarcane growers, sugar millers, sugar industry workers

policydecision_details: The President of the United States has issued a proclamation to impose significant ad valorem duties on imported unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and their components. A 100 percent duty rate applies to UAS with a maximum take-off weight exceeding 25 kilograms, those with thermal imagers, and specific docking stations. A 25 percent duty rate is applied to smaller UAS and certain other components. These measures are designed to reduce reliance on foreign supply chains and incentivize the onshoring of domestic manufacturing capacity. The policy also authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to expand the scope of these tariffs on a rolling basis to address ongoing national security risks.
contextoradditionalinfo: An investigation under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 concluded that the United States is overly reliant on foreign sources for UAS technology, which is critical for military, law enforcement, and commercial applications including agriculture. The report identified significant cybersecurity risks associated with foreign-manufactured UAS software and noted that current domestic production capacity is insufficient to meet national security needs. The reliance on foreign supply chains for components like motors and batteries was deemed a strategic vulnerability that could be exploited during geopolitical events or natural disasters.
beneficiaries: domestic UAS manufacturers, defense industrial base

policydecision_details: The European Union will suspend imports of animal-origin products from Brazil starting Thursday, September 3, after saying the country failed to prove control over the use of antimicrobials in local production chains. The EU ban on Brazilian animal products will apply to beef, poultry, eggs, honey and fish.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: China has agreed to implement a Tk10,000 crore modern housing project to rehabilitate slum dwellers in the Dhaka-17 constituency. The project involves constructing 20-storey buildings where residents can live rent-free while covering only utility costs. Additionally, the initiative includes investments in waste-to-energy and renewable energy projects, such as the Aminbazar landfill electricity generation plant. A tripartite agreement for these developments is scheduled to be signed in Beijing on September 2, 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project aims to improve living conditions for residents of the Korail, Sat Tala, and Bhashantek slums in Dhaka. It is part of a broader bilateral cooperation effort between China and Bangladesh involving infrastructure, energy, and urban development. The initiative seeks to address urban poverty and improve access to essential services like electricity and sanitation.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The government of Uzbekistan has announced a policy initiative to increase public-sector wages. The measure also includes the introduction of new subsidies and the implementation of updated bus fare regulations. These changes are intended to adjust the economic conditions for public employees and manage public transport costs. The announcement was reported by the 'Daryo' online publication.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy reflects ongoing administrative and economic adjustments within Uzbekistan's public sector. The information provided is limited to the announcement of these measures without specific details on the scale of wage increases or the nature of the new subsidies.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The government of Uzbekistan has announced a strategic shift in its nuclear energy project, effectively downgrading the role of the Russian entity Rosatom. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has endorsed the creation of a new consortium to oversee construction, aiming to improve project management and conduct independent technical assessments. The government intends to increase the share of domestic participation in the project, targeting 30 percent local production and 65 percent of construction work to be handled by national enterprises. Additionally, a manufacturing complex will be established near the site to produce necessary building materials and components locally.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision follows growing tensions in Uzbek-Russian relations and dissatisfaction with the original financing and management plans proposed by Rosatom. Uzbekistan is seeking to reduce its reliance on the Russian entity while simultaneously exploring potential nuclear energy cooperation with other international partners, including the United States. The project, which includes two 1 gigawatt reactors and two smaller 55 megawatt models, faces significant financing challenges, leading the government to prioritize local economic benefits and job creation.

policydecision_details: The Hungarian government has announced plans to introduce a new wealth tax targeting individuals with assets exceeding 1 billion forint ($3.1 million). This measure is part of a broader initiative to increase levies on the country's wealthiest citizens. According to Cabinet Minister Balint Ruff, the regulation has been prepared for some time and is intended to be a milestone in the country's fiscal policy. The tax will apply to both income and assets that surpass the specified threshold.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is being promoted by Prime Minister Peter Magyar as part of a strategy to address wealth inequality and increase tax revenue from the richest segments of the population.

policydecision_details: The National Development Planning Commission (NDPC) of Ghana is developing four new regulatory measures to address public health concerns related to nutrition. These measures include restrictions on food advertising, the implementation of front-of-pack nutrition labelling, the introduction of food-related taxes, and new regulations for food provided in public institutions. The commission is currently engaging with industry stakeholders, including the Association of Ghana Industries and Coca-Cola Ghana, to discuss the potential impact of these policies. Regulatory impact assessments and further consultations are planned before the final implementation of these measures.

The Iraqi Cabinet has implemented a temporary ban on agricultural imports. This measure is intended to remain in effect until the conclusion of the current domestic production season. The decision aims to protect local farmers and encourage the consumption of domestic agricultural output. Additionally, the Cabinet approved a draft law to establish a Food and Drug Authority to further regulate the sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to support local production and enhance food security by reducing reliance on foreign agricultural imports during the peak domestic harvest season. This is part of a broader government strategy to boost domestic food production and improve regulatory oversight through the creation of a new national authority.

policydecision_details: The Macao University of Tourism (UTM) and Xia Ding Technology Co., Ltd. have launched an industry-academia-research project to develop AI-assisted dining solutions using AR smart glasses. The project aims to create an intelligent service interaction system that replaces traditional dining service models with a more efficient, tech-driven experience. Research and testing are being conducted at the UTM Educational Restaurant to refine service logic and scenario adaptation. The initiative seeks to provide a practical model for the high-quality development of Macao’s tourism and hospitality sectors.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is part of the Macao SAR Government’s broader strategy to promote smart tourism and cultivate new productive forces within the region. By integrating augmented reality (AR) and artificial intelligence (AI) into the dining experience, the government aims to modernize the local hotel, food-and-beverage, and integrated tourism service industries to maintain competitiveness.
beneficiaries: hotel sector, food-and-beverage sector, tourism service sector

policydecision_details: The Macao SAR Government held an investment promotion seminar in Jakarta, Indonesia, to strengthen economic and trade ties. The event facilitated 120 business matching sessions and resulted in the signing of 36 cooperation agreements. These agreements cover sectors including tourism, MICE, high technology, traditional Chinese medicine, and Big Health. The initiative aims to leverage Macao's role as a platform between the Chinese mainland and Portuguese-speaking countries to foster two-way investment.
contextoradditionalinfo: The seminar is part of the Macao SAR Government’s Third Five-Year Plan and the '1+4' industrial diversification strategy. It seeks to expand Macao's economic cooperation network with Southeast Asia, specifically Indonesia, which is a major visitor market and a key ASEAN economy. The initiative also promotes the 'Macao + Hengqin' joint development model to attract international investment.

policydecision_details: The government of Curaçao has announced a plan to replace its aging GOS tax administration computer system by the end of 2028. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to improve the reliability, auditability, and lawfulness of government tax revenue reporting. The current system, which accounts for tax receipts on a cash basis, is deemed insufficient for modern requirements. The modernization effort is a key component of the government's roadmap to obtain an unqualified audit opinion on its annual accounts.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision stems from ongoing uncertainty regarding the completeness and accuracy of tax revenues recorded in the government's accounts. The Financial Management Report of June 2026 highlighted the need for this technological upgrade to ensure that the Tax Administration's processes are properly supported. The project is considered significant due to the large volume of public funds processed through the tax system, which exceeded projections in the first half of 2026.

policydecision_details: The Curaçao government has announced a review of the AOV pension system as a core component of its new social policy. This initiative aims to combat poverty and ensure that elderly residents can live with dignity. The government intends to adopt an integrated approach that connects income, employment, housing, and healthcare to improve the daily lives of residents. Public resources will be prioritized toward areas of greatest need to ensure economic progress translates into tangible improvements for families and seniors.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in the government program presented by Governor Mauritsz de Kort at the opening of the 2026–2027 parliamentary year. It responds to rising concerns regarding poverty, housing shortages, and the high cost of living on the island. The government emphasizes that social challenges are interconnected and require a holistic strategy to support vulnerable populations.

policydecision_details: The Chinese government has ended a 32-year-old dividend tax exemption for foreign individuals. Effective September 1, 2026, foreign shareholders and executives are now subject to a 20 percent withholding tax on dividends received from foreign-invested enterprises.
