The intervention aims to restore damaged water infrastructure, improve access to irrigation water, strengthen agricultural production, and enhance the resilience and livelihoods of farmers affected by land destruction and attacks in the area.

The Jordanian-Palestinian Agricultural Products Marketing Company signed agreements to export and market 1,700 tonnes of Palestinian agricultural products, including avocados, lemons, dates, and other produce, to markets in Jordan and the UAE. The agreements aim to open new marketing channels, increase demand for Palestinian products, improve market access and returns for farmers, and strengthen partnerships that support the resilience and continued production of Palestinian farmers. The initiative also seeks to expand export volumes, diversify targeted agricultural products, and increase the contribution of agriculture to the Palestinian economy.

Oman plans to develop a wheat grain storage facility in Ibra, North Al Sharqiyah Governorate, to expand national grain-handling capacity and improve the storage and distribution of wheat. The project forms part of broader efforts to strengthen food supply systems, reduce risks associated with dependence on imported food, and improve grain logistics and infrastructure. The investment also complements Oman’s wider development of milling, port, agricultural, and transport infrastructure, while potentially supporting the country’s role in regional grain trade and distribution.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: The Israeli government has issued tenders for the construction of 1,234 housing units in the E1 area of the West Bank. This project is part of a larger plan to build 3,401 units in a strategically sensitive region east of Jerusalem. The tender process is scheduled to conclude on October 19, 2026, shortly before the national general election. This move is intended to solidify settlement expansion and create physical barriers between the northern and southern parts of the West Bank.
contextoradditionalinfo: The E1 area is considered critical for the potential establishment of a contiguous Palestinian state. International observers and the UN have long condemned development in this area, warning that it would bisect the West Bank and isolate East Jerusalem. The current Israeli government has explicitly stated that the project aims to erase the possibility of a two-state solution. The decision has faced significant international backlash, including condemnation from the UK government.

policydecision_details: The Government of Ecuador, under the administration of Daniel Noboa, has invested USD 2.5 million in the modernization and upgrading of the Orthotics and Prosthetics Laboratory at the Isidro Ayora General Hospital in Loja. This investment aims to improve the quality and availability of specialized medical devices for patients in the region. The project focuses on enhancing the technical capabilities of the laboratory to better serve the local population. This initiative is part of the Ministry of Public Health's efforts to strengthen public health infrastructure.
contextoradditionalinfo: The investment is intended to address the need for improved medical rehabilitation services and specialized equipment in the Loja province, ensuring that patients have better access to essential orthotic and prosthetic care.

policydecision_details: The Ecuadorian government, through the Ministry of Public Health, has launched an initiative to strengthen breastfeeding education and counseling by distributing 2,787 didactic kits. These kits, funded by the Inter-American Development Bank, will be deployed to first-level health establishments in prioritized parishes nationwide. Health personnel will utilize these resources to provide practical guidance to parents and caregivers on breastfeeding and infant nutrition. This intervention aims to improve exclusive breastfeeding rates and support the healthy development of children during their first 1,000 days of life.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of the National Strategy 'Ecuador Grows without Child Malnutrition' (ENECSDI) and addresses the urgent need to combat Chronic Childhood Malnutrition (CIM). Recent data from the National Survey on Child Malnutrition (ENDI) 2023-2024 indicates that while 53.1% of children under six months receive exclusive breastfeeding, there is significant room for improvement in maintaining these practices. By providing better educational tools, the government seeks to increase the adoption of exclusive breastfeeding and appropriate complementary feeding practices to reduce malnutrition rates.
beneficiaries: pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, fathers, caregivers of children under two years of age

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The Greater Amman Municipality has approved new regulations for the sale, trading, storage, and transportation of horticultural products. The policy mandates that all such products must be supplied through the central market or an approved electronic platform. It establishes specific criteria for exempting perishable goods and those intended for food processing from central market requirements. Sellers are required to maintain and present official documentation for all transactions to ensure regulatory compliance. The measure aims to strengthen oversight and document the movement of horticultural products within municipal boundaries.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to regulate the horticultural market, improve oversight of product movement, and reduce undocumented trading. By requiring official documentation and central market processing, the municipality seeks to ensure compliance with legislation and improve the transparency of the supply chain for fruits and vegetables.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: The Government of Mexico City has issued a decree to reform the Urban Garden Law, integrating the Ministry of Education, Science, Technology and Innovation into the framework. The policy mandates the promotion of urban garden development and vegetable cultivation within basic education curricula. It establishes a requirement for the Secretariat to coordinate with schools to deliver training workshops on environmental education and urban agriculture. This initiative aims to foster agricultural knowledge and food production skills among students.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decree is part of an effort to institutionalize environmental and agricultural education within the Mexico City school system, leveraging the Urban Garden Law to promote sustainable food practices and urban greening.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Croatian Government has approved an initial €20 million (USD 23 million) emergency aid package to support the city of Omiš following a devastating wildfire. The funds are designated for the removal and repair of fire-related damage, with further assistance planned as damage assessments continue. The package includes tax relief for residents and businesses, support for the local economy, and specific aid for farmers and war veterans. Additionally, the Ministry of Culture and Media will oversee the restoration of damaged cultural assets.
contextoradditionalinfo: A major wildfire occurred in the Omiš area in August 2026, causing an estimated €110 million in damages to properties, infrastructure, and the local economy. The government intervention aims to provide immediate relief to the affected population and facilitate the recovery of the region.
beneficiaries: residents of Omiš, businesses, farmers, war veterans
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Government of Pakistan has authorized the export of 108,000 metric tonnes of sugar that was previously imported. The Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) has been directed to invite international tenders to facilitate this sale. This decision follows failed attempts to sell the stock domestically due to lower market prices. The move is intended to clear surplus stocks held by the TCP.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision was made despite concerns regarding potential local price escalation and a breach of commitments to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to end government market intervention. The sugar was originally imported to address domestic shortages, but subsequent production improvements and market dynamics led to a surplus of the imported commodity. The government previously waived 53% of import taxes to facilitate the initial import, which has been a point of contention.

policydecision_details: The Sixth amendment to the Income Tax Regulation introduces several modifications to tax registration, withholding tax requirements, and accounting procedures. It mandates registration for individuals earning over MVR 60,000 monthly and those required to deduct non-resident or capital gains withholding tax. The amendment also clarifies the definition of remuneration regarding accommodation benefits and updates rules for currency conversion and partnership dissolution. Furthermore, it adjusts the computation of employee withholding tax for high-income earners and establishes new guidelines for operating lease deductions.
contextoradditionalinfo: This regulation is part of the ongoing refinement of the Maldives' income tax framework, aimed at improving tax compliance, clarifying definitions for remuneration and benefits, and streamlining administrative procedures for businesses and individuals.

policydecision_details: The U.S. Department of Labor has issued a final rule removing the requirement for States to use State merit staff to provide Wagner-Peyser Employment Service (ES) services. This change grants States the flexibility to determine the most efficient and cost-effective staffing model for delivering these labor exchange services. The rule aims to modernize the operation of public employment offices by allowing for alternative staffing arrangements. This policy shift is effective as of October 19, 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Wagner-Peyser Act of 1933 established a nationwide program of labor exchange services to match job seekers with employers. Historically, the Department of Labor required States to use merit-based staff to operate these services to ensure uniformity and efficiency. This new rule reflects a shift toward deregulation and increased operational flexibility for States in managing their workforce development programs.

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture (Palestine), in cooperation with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), signed 18 agreements supporting agricultural investment projects under the Multi-Donor Agricultural Business Program (MAP II). The projects, valued at approximately 5.9 million shekels, aim to promote market-oriented investment and innovation, increase agricultural production, support individual and cooperative enterprises, create employment opportunities, and strengthen farmers’ resilience and access to markets. The initiative is funded by multiple international partners and includes monitoring and supervision by the Ministry and FAO to ensure effective implementation and sustainable impacts on the Palestinian agri-food sector.

The ministry set maximum selling prices for selected poultry products, including live and ready-to-cook chicken, while requiring market stakeholders to maintain regular supplies, comply with traceability requirements, and ensure adequate availability of cut-up chicken. The measure aims to regulate poultry prices and support market supply, although enforcement may remain challenging.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Trade and Export Development

policydecision_details: OCP has resumed shipments of 54,000 tonnes of Triple Super Phosphate (TSP) fertilizer to the United States, reopening a supply route that had been largely inactive for more than five years. The shipment is expected to increase phosphate fertilizer availability ahead of the US fall application season, while temporary relief from US countervailing duties allows OCP to re-enter the market and provides farmers with a more diversified supply source. The move comes amid concerns about fertilizer supply disruptions and limited domestic production in the US.

Egypt procured 4.72 million tonnes of wheat from the domestic harvest, an increase from the previous season, as part of efforts to reduce dependence on imports and strengthen national food security. The government is supporting domestic wheat production through higher procurement prices, improved seeds, expanded cultivation on reclaimed land, and modern farming practices such as laser land levelling. When durum wheat purchased by pasta factories and wheat retained for seed is included, total procurement reportedly exceeded the 5 million-tonne target, supporting Egypt’s longer-term goal of achieving greater wheat self-sufficiency for the subsidized bread programme.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade

policydecision_details: Kuwait Customs seized 2,236 items of subsidized and rationed food supplies from six containers at Shuwaikh Port that were being prepared for export to Sri Lanka. The shipment included subsidized milk, flour, oil, ghee, lentils, pasta, rice, sugar, and tomato paste. The seizure is part of efforts to protect Kuwait’s food security, safeguard strategic stocks of essential commodities, ensure subsidized products reach their intended beneficiaries, and prevent their illegal export.

The Minister and Commissioner for Food Security, Mr. Redouwane AG MOHAMED ALI, officially launched the 2026 Free Food Distribution operations in the Timbuktu region. The initiative aims to provide food assistance to 134,366 vulnerable individuals through the distribution of 1,801 tonnes of cereals. Additionally, the program includes the provision of 18 tonnes of fish feed and 600 boxes of vegetable seeds to support local production and livelihoods. This effort is part of a broader strategy to strengthen the national response to food and nutritional insecurity while fostering resilience among vulnerable populations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The mission was conducted to address food and nutritional insecurity in the Timbuktu region, following a similar operation in the Kayes region. The government, in collaboration with the World Food Programme (WFP), seeks to improve the living conditions of populations and support local agricultural production to enhance long-term resilience.

policydecision_details: The Government of The Gambia has launched the African Manufacturers and Makers (AFRIMMAK) programme to foster an enabling environment for young entrepreneurs and startups. The initiative provides mentorship, networking, entrepreneurship education, and leadership development to empower youth as active participants in the economy. It was officially inaugurated with the Young Innovators Challenge, a competition designed to build business skills among students. The programme aims to strengthen the national entrepreneurial ecosystem and encourage innovation from an early age.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of a broader government strategy to build a competitive, inclusive, and investment-driven economy. It complements existing government efforts such as the Digital Single Window for business registration, the She Trades Gambia Hub, and the National Standards Initiative. By nurturing local talent and innovation, the government seeks to prepare young Gambians to leverage opportunities within the African Continental Free Trade Area.

policydecision_details: The Croatian government has officially commenced the construction of the second and third phases of the Drniš bypass. This infrastructure project involves an investment of USD 45 million and is expected to take 30 months to complete. The bypass includes the construction of overpasses, viaducts, and a bridge over the Čikola River. The project aims to reduce through traffic in the town and improve regional connectivity.
contextoradditionalinfo: The bypass is a strategic infrastructure development intended to improve road connections between the coast, inland Dalmatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is also designed to support economic development by linking the Drniš industrial zone to the Port of Šibenik, thereby increasing regional business competitiveness.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure
beneficiaries: local businesses, transport sector, residents of Šibenik-Knin County

policydecision_details: The Russian Federation transferred 556 tons of food, including yellow split peas and sunflower oil, to Burkina Faso as humanitarian aid. This delivery was organized in collaboration with the UN World Food Programme (WFP) as part of an additional voluntary contribution. The aid is intended to support vulnerable populations affected by the activities of terrorist groups. The initiative aims to strengthen food sovereignty and combat hunger in the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The humanitarian aid was provided in response to food insecurity in Burkina Faso, exacerbated by the activities of terrorist groups. The assistance is part of Russia's broader humanitarian policy and its cooperation with African nations to address food security and sovereignty challenges.
decision_making_institution: Embassy of the Russian Federation in Ouagadougou

policydecision_details: The Parliamentary Public Accounts Committee has approved amendments to the Foreign Exchange Bill that criminalize the advertising or promotion of foreign currency exchange rates exceeding limits set by the Maldives Monetary Authority. The measure imposes significant fines on individuals and businesses that publish or disseminate information regarding unauthorized exchange rates. These amendments also mandate that all foreign currency transactions must occur within the bands established by the central bank. The bill is currently proceeding through the parliamentary process following a review.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government introduced these measures to curb market instability caused by the circulation of black market dollar rates. Economic officials expressed concern that media reporting on these unofficial rates negatively impacts the small Maldivian economy. The legislation aims to centralize control over foreign exchange information and trading practices to stabilize the national currency market.
beneficiaries: foreign currency traders, media outlets, registered businesses

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy, Addu Equatorial Hospital, and WAMCO have signed a tripartite Memorandum of Understanding to establish a pilot cytotoxic waste treatment and storage facility in Addu City. This facility will utilize a non-burn treatment method involving soda lime and cement encapsulation to safely manage hazardous chemotherapy waste. The project aims to test operational arrangements and provide a model for other healthcare facilities across the Maldives. Construction has commenced at the designated site in Hithadhoo, with the facility expected to be operational within 2026.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy
beneficiaries: healthcare workers, waste management workers, local communities

policydecision_details: The Libyan Medical Supply Organisation has launched the first National Formulary to standardize the selection, procurement, and use of prescription medications. This official list includes generic and brand-name drugs evaluated for safety, effectiveness, and cost-efficiency. The policy establishes a unified national reference to guide the entire drug management cycle, from supply to patient administration. By defining approved medications, the formulary directly influences import decisions and pharmaceutical market access. This initiative aims to reform the pharmaceutical system and enhance national drug security.

policy_description: Local production of fertilizers and other agricultural inputs
policydecision_details: Egypt has officially begun the construction of a USD 658 million phosphoric acid production complex located on the Abu Tartour mining plateau. The project is a collaborative effort involving state-owned companies and local financial institutions, with construction expected to span 30 months. The facility aims to process locally mined phosphate rock into high-concentration commercial phosphoric acid. This initiative is designed to shift the country's strategy from exporting raw minerals to downstream processing, thereby increasing value-added output. The plant is expected to generate significant foreign currency earnings and create over 3,000 jobs.
contextoradditionalinfo: Egypt holds the world's third-largest phosphate reserves and is actively seeking to maximize the economic value derived from these natural resources. The government is prioritizing downstream industrialization to support macroeconomic stability and reduce reliance on raw material exports. This project is part of a broader national strategy to expand the domestic chemical and fertilizer manufacturing sector through partnerships with both local and international investors.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources
policycategory: Local production of fertilizers and other agricultural inputs

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: Mongolia has officially launched its National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan for 2026–2030. The strategy aims to translate global biodiversity commitments into concrete national results. Key objectives include strengthening policy synergy across international conventions and enhancing ecosystem resilience against desertification and climate change. The plan also focuses on expanding protected areas and promoting community-based conservation to support sustainable livelihoods.
contextoradditionalinfo: The strategy was developed to align Mongolia's national efforts with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework established in 2022. It serves as a continuation of Mongolia's commitment to the Convention on Biological Diversity, which the country joined in 1993. The policy was formally enacted by a Government Resolution on June 10, 2026, to address environmental degradation and biodiversity loss.
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine has updated the regulatory framework for auctions used to distribute quotas for renewable energy projects. These new procedures are designed to simplify the investment process and increase the profitability of green energy initiatives. The government aims to boost domestic electricity production through these auctions to enhance national energy resilience. The updated auction process is scheduled to commence this autumn.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy update is a strategic response to ongoing attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, which have threatened the country's energy security. By incentivizing investment in renewable energy, the government seeks to decentralize and strengthen the power generation capacity of the nation.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine has temporarily adjusted the minimum allowable export prices for specific agricultural products. This decision aims to make export contracts economically viable again by accounting for rising logistics costs and declining domestic purchase prices. The measure is designed to prevent the suspension of grain and oilseed exports. It serves as the first step in a broader emergency support package for the agricultural sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to ongoing Russian attacks in the Black Sea, which have severely impacted the agricultural sector. Previous minimum price requirements had become unattainable for producers, threatening the continuity of exports. The government is monitoring the situation daily and preparing further stabilization measures.

policydecision_details: The EU has introduced new marketing and labelling requirements that restrict the use of meat-related terminology for plant-based and alternative protein products. Terms such as 'meat', 'steak', 'bacon', and 'fillet' are now reserved exclusively for animal-derived products. A transitional period is provided for businesses to update their packaging, with a final deadline for non-compliant stock set for August 19th, 2032. The regulation also empowers the European Commission to extend origin labelling requirements to poultry meat and spreadable fats.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy aims to improve consumer clarity by preventing the potential misleading use of traditional meat terminology on non-meat products. By distinguishing between animal-based and alternative products, the regulation seeks to ensure transparency in food labelling across the EU market.
commodity3: Others meat or animal derived products

policydecision_details: The government of Uzbekistan has announced the launch of the 'Export Navigator' program. This initiative is designed to serve as a component of a broader business support package aimed at facilitating international trade. The program seeks to assist local businesses in navigating export processes more effectively. It represents a strategic effort to enhance the country's export capabilities and economic growth.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a wider government strategy to provide comprehensive support to the business sector in Uzbekistan, specifically focusing on improving export performance and market access.

This initiative is designed to serve as a component of a broader business support package aimed at facilitating international trade. The program seeks to assist local businesses in navigating export processes more effectively. It represents a strategic effort to enhance the country's export capabilities and economic growth.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a wider government strategy to provide comprehensive support to the business sector in Uzbekistan, specifically focusing on improving export performance and market access.

policydecision_details: The Central Bank of Tunisia revised the financing scales for cereal and selected seasonal crops, establishing updated bank credit ceilings based on crop type, production zone, and whether land is irrigated or rainfed. The revised framework covers durum and soft wheat, legumes, barley, and forage crops, with financing levels adjusted according to farm size, expected production costs, and previous yields. The measure aims to improve access to agricultural finance and ensure that bank lending better reflects regional and production conditions.

The Iraqi Cabinet has approved an advance-payment system for customs duties and tax deposits on imported goods. Importers are now required to deposit funds with licensed banks before transferring money abroad for imports. The system utilizes the ASYCUDA platform to calculate estimated duties based on commercial invoices and product classification. This measure aims to automate customs procedures and ensure the collection of state revenue.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader customs automation program intended to modernize trade procedures and increase non-oil revenue. It also serves to protect domestic production by applying specific tariff classifications to imports. Traders have expressed concerns regarding the financial burden of upfront payments and the lack of corresponding improvements in public services.

policy_description: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements
policydecision_details: The South African government and the Citrus Growers’ Association have secured approval from India for additional fruit fly cold treatment options for fresh citrus exports. This regulatory adjustment improves technical market access conditions for South African producers. The measure aims to enhance the quality of fruit exported to India and provide greater logistical flexibility for exporters. This development is part of a broader strategy to diversify export markets and increase the presence of South African citrus in the Indian economy.
contextoradditionalinfo: South Africa has been negotiating with Indian authorities for nearly a decade to improve phytosanitary access for citrus. While South Africa already exports citrus to India, current trade is limited by existing treatment protocols and high Most-Favoured-Nation tariffs. The industry seeks to leverage India's growing middle class and demand for high-quality produce to ensure long-term sustainability and diversification of the sector.
decision_making_institution: Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development
policycategory: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries announced the prices of certified and controlled cereal seeds for the upcoming 2026–2027 agricultural season, setting prices for durum wheat, soft wheat, barley, and triticale seeds and applying an additional surcharge to certified varieties subject to plant variety rights. The ministry is also ensuring the availability of sufficient quantities of certified and ordinary seeds through designated sales points as part of preparations for the next cereal sowing campaign and to support farmers’ access to quality planting material.

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: The Jordan Valley Authority, in partnership with the Netherlands and the IUCN, has launched a 10-million-euro project to mitigate siltation in the King Talal Dam basin. The initiative employs an integrated strategy combining engineering and nature-based solutions to address soil erosion at its source. By treating sediment sources in the upper catchment area, the project aims to safeguard water resources and optimize the efficiency of storage infrastructure. The project is scheduled to run for four years with the goal of reducing sediment inflow into the reservoir by at least 10 percent.
contextoradditionalinfo: King Talal Dam is a vital surface water storage facility for Jordan, providing essential irrigation water to farmers in the Jordan Valley. The dam has been facing significant siltation issues, which threaten its storage capacity and, consequently, national water security. This project aligns with Jordan's National Water Strategy 2023–2040 and addresses the urgent need to manage water scarcity and climate change impacts.
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration is deploying four new temporary humanitarian assistance sites in Ceuta to support migrants. These facilities, including the Loma Colmenar car park and the Cavalry Barracks, will provide an initial capacity for 1,500 people. The government has also endorsed an emergency declaration of 6.5 million euros (USD 7.6 million) to facilitate support through the Red Cross. This initiative aims to ensure proper humanitarian care and protect the fundamental rights of vulnerable individuals in the city.
contextoradditionalinfo: The measure was introduced to address the urgent humanitarian situation in the Autonomous City of Ceuta, where there is a high demand for reception spaces and basic needs support for migrants. The government is collaborating with local authorities and the Red Cross to manage the influx and provide essential services, including daily food and hygiene kits.
decision_making_institution: Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: The Bolivian government issued Decreto Supremo 5676 to end diesel subsidies for large consumers, effectively doubling their fuel costs to address a structural crisis in the hydrocarbons sector. Simultaneously, the government launched the second phase of the BOL-38 emergency employment program, investing US$92.7 million in municipal paving works. This dual approach aims to reduce fiscal pressure from fuel subsidies while stimulating job creation through local infrastructure projects. Small producers remain protected by a subsidized fuel allowance to mitigate the impact on the rural economy.
contextoradditionalinfo: Bolivia is facing a structural crisis in its hydrocarbons sector, characterized by a significant decline in domestic production and a heavy reliance on fuel imports. The government has struggled to balance the financial burden of subsidizing fuel prices against the need to maintain public accounts. The new measures are designed to stabilize the state energy company YPFB while providing immediate economic relief through targeted employment initiatives.
beneficiaries: small producers, municipal governments, indigenous autonomous governments
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: The Government of Lesotho has received 100,000 doses of Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) vaccines from Botswana to combat a national outbreak. This initiative includes a collaborative training program where veterinary experts from Botswana will train local staff on vaccination procedures. Following the training, a nationwide livestock vaccination campaign will be launched to contain the disease. The government is also actively seeking additional vaccine supplies to expand the program and restore the country's FMD-free status.
contextoradditionalinfo: The vaccine donation is a direct outcome of the Inaugural Lesotho–Botswana Bi-National Commission (BNC), which aimed to strengthen cooperation in animal health, disease surveillance, and food security. The measure is intended to protect the livelihoods of Basotho farmers and support the national livestock sector against the current FMD outbreak.

policydecision_details: The Greek government has launched a National Housing Policy Strategy for 2026–2035, comprising 50 measures to address the housing crisis. Key initiatives include expanding the 'My Home' programme with tax incentives for banks offering reduced-rate loans and introducing a new Golden Visa category for long-term rental investments. The strategy also proposes preferential support for developers who provide social or affordable housing and establishes a national price index for transparency. While the strategy is approved, most measures require separate legislation and technical implementation before they become fully operational.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address the ongoing housing crisis in Greece, characterized by rising property prices and limited availability of affordable long-term rental options. The government aims to unlock the housing market by incentivizing supply and providing financial support to specific demographics, including students and essential public-sector workers.

policydecision_details: The National Drug Policy of Panama 2026-2036 was officially launched by the National Commission for the Study and Prevention of Drugs (CONAPRED). This comprehensive policy aims to address the drug phenomenon through a dual approach of demand reduction and supply control. Key priorities include prevention efforts focused on the youth population and the recovery and labor integration of individuals treated for drug use. The policy also emphasizes inter-institutional cooperation to mitigate the negative impacts of drugs on health, security, and governance.
contextoradditionalinfo: The new policy serves as an update to the strategic framework established in the National Drug Strategy 2012-2017. It was developed to align with international commitments and to incorporate modern monitoring methodologies and public policy standards. The initiative seeks to address the drug phenomenon in a more comprehensive manner, respecting human rights, diversity, and gender perspectives.
decision_making_institution: National Commission for the Study and Prevention of Drugs (CONAPRED)
beneficiaries: youth population, people treated for drug use

policydecision_details: Cambodia and Singapore launched a five-day training program to enhance food safety and processing standards for Cambodian officials. The initiative focuses on food safety management, storage, value addition, and sustainable production methods. It aims to improve the competitiveness of Cambodian agricultural products in both domestic and international markets. The program also covers product standardization, classification, and quality improvement to reduce post-harvest losses.
contextoradditionalinfo: The training was organized in response to the Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation's (MISTI) priorities to strengthen Cambodia's food production capacity. By adopting international standards and improving processing techniques, the government seeks to protect public health and build long-term consumer confidence. This collaboration is part of the Singapore Cooperation Programme, aimed at deepening bilateral cooperation and addressing Cambodia's specific needs in the agricultural sector.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation (MISTI)

policydecision_details: The Tripartite National Committee for Labor and Social Partnership has decided to increase Mongolia’s minimum wage by 26.3%. The monthly minimum wage will rise from MNT 792,000 to MNT 1 million (USD 278), effective January 1, 2027. Additionally, the hourly minimum wage will be set at MNT 5,952.30. This decision was reached following a meeting held between August 14 and August 17, 2026.
decision_making_institution: Tripartite National Committee for Labor and Social Partnership

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Environment Protection Fund approved a package of environmental and development projects focused on protecting natural resources, strengthening food security, supporting rural communities, and promoting sustainable development. The projects include water-harvesting wells and home gardens, renewable-energy-based drying of vegetables and fruits, rehabilitation of nature reserves and wetlands, development of the Mujib Agricultural Project as a model for modern agriculture, establishment of an applied agricultural academy for innovative and environmentally friendly farming, expansion of green spaces, and recycling plastic into public-use products. The initiatives also aim to empower youth and women, create livelihood opportunities, strengthen local community participation, and advance the green and circular economies.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Education and Higher Education has expanded its education voucher initiative by offering 3,793 places for Qatari students at 17 private schools. The initiative covers tuition fees up to QR28,000 annually, with participating schools absorbing any costs exceeding this amount. Eligibility has been broadened by removing the previous monthly income limit of QR35,000. This measure aims to enhance educational access and social support for Qatari families. Previously rejected applicants due to income constraints are now being reviewed and offered placements.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader social responsibility initiative by the Ministry of Education and Higher Education to ensure Qatari students have access to private education without additional financial burden on parents. This aligns with national efforts to improve social inclusion and human capital development.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Education and Higher Education

policydecision_details: The Ministry has approved updated executive regulations for monitoring and enforcing water-efficiency and conservation standards, empowering the National Water Efficiency and Conservation Center to investigate violations across the urban, agricultural, and industrial sectors. The rules introduce escalating fines for using inefficient sanitary fixtures, tampering with water-saving components, wasting drinking water due to defective or poorly maintained tanks, and using drinking water for purposes where alternative sources such as treated wastewater or licensed wells are available. Penalties range from SR500 to SR200,000, strengthening enforcement of water conservation and supporting the sustainable management of Saudi Arabia’s scarce water resources.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policydecision_details: The UAE is expanding its network of Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements (CEPAs) to diversify export markets, reduce trade barriers, strengthen private-sector competitiveness, and expand investment and trade links across Asia, Africa, and Europe. Since the programme was launched in 2021, the UAE has signed 38 CEPAs, with an increasing number entering into force and improving market access for UAE businesses. The agreements are supporting opportunities in sectors including agriculture, logistics, renewable energy, manufacturing, and investment, while strengthening the UAE’s role as a global trade and logistics hub connecting Asian, African, and European markets.
decision_making_institution: UAE Ministry of Economy and Tourism

policydecision_details: Fiji has officially launched its Horizon 2030 Food Systems Strategy and National Agrifood Investment Plan to unify national priorities regarding food security, agriculture, and nutrition. The strategy provides a long-term strategic direction, while the investment plan outlines a FJD 26.5 million (USD 11.7 million) envelope to support governance, value chain development, and climate resilience. The initiative involves a multi-stakeholder framework including government ministries, UN agencies, and the private sector to transition from planning to active implementation. This effort aims to transform Fiji's agrifood system into a more resilient, nature-positive, and nutrition-sensitive model.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was developed to address climate and economic challenges facing Fiji's food systems. It aligns with the UN Food Systems Transformation agenda and seeks to improve rural livelihoods and food security through coordinated national and international support, including funding from the European Union.
beneficiaries: smallholder farmers, rural households, private sector

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: Effective August 14, 2026, the Customs of the People's Republic of China has implemented anti-dumping duties on imports of single-mode optical fiber originating from India. The duty is levied ad valorem based on the customs-determined taxable value of the imported goods. Additionally, an import value-added tax is applied to the taxable value, which includes both customs duties and the newly imposed anti-dumping duties. This measure is designed to protect domestic industry from unfair pricing practices.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader set of trade defense measures aimed at stabilizing the competitive environment for domestic industries, specifically within the electronics and ICT sectors, by addressing dumped imports.
decision_making_institution: Customs of the People's Republic of China
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
commodity1: Other products, not included in the other categories

policydecision_details: The government, in collaboration with Action Aid International The Gambia and local youth committees, initiated a tree-planting project in Amdalai village. Over 400 trees were planted to serve as a natural windbreak and climate-mitigation measure following a devastating storm. This initiative aims to protect homes, farms, and local infrastructure from future extreme weather events. The project also focuses on long-term environmental sustainability and socio-economic development for the community.
contextoradditionalinfo: A powerful windstorm in Amdalai village destroyed roofs and damaged over 15 households, exposing the community's vulnerability due to a lack of surrounding vegetation. The initiative was launched as a direct response to this disaster to address underlying environmental risks and enhance climate resilience.

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry of Japan has introduced disaster relief measures to support local businesses impacted by heavy rainfall. The policy provides loan guarantees to assist small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the affected municipalities. This intervention aims to mitigate the economic disruption caused by the severe weather event that began on 13 August 2026. The measure is part of the government's broader disaster response framework to ensure business continuity in the Chiba region.
contextoradditionalinfo: On 13 August 2026, heavy rain caused significant damage across 25 municipalities in Chiba, Japan. In response to the resulting economic hardship for local businesses, the government implemented targeted financial support to facilitate recovery and stability for affected SMEs.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry

policydecision_details: The Ukrainian government has introduced measures to support the agricultural sector by expanding credit and guarantee facilities. Farmers can now access up to UAH 90 million (USD 2 million) in working capital loans, with UAH 20.8 billion allocated for portfolio guarantees under the 'Affordable Loans at 5-7-9%' program. The National Bank of Ukraine has increased the collateral ratio for agricultural products from 0.4 to 0.75 to boost financing capacity. Additionally, lending requirements, including restructuring and performance assessments, have been eased until September 1, 2027. These actions aim to sustain agricultural exports and support autumn fieldwork despite ongoing logistical challenges.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to the blockade of maritime logistics, particularly the Odesa ports, which has severely hampered agricultural exports. With only 30% of required export volumes achieved in early August, the government is attempting to mitigate the risk of up to 30 million tonnes of agricultural potential failing to reach global markets. The measures are designed to maintain export capacity through alternative routes and ensure the continuity of agricultural production.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The UNDP in Uzbekistan and the National Agency for Energy Efficiency conducted a series of training sessions for 80 specialists to enhance energy auditing skills. The training focused on the ESCO model, covering legal and technical foundations, baseline energy consumption assessment, and verification methods. Participants from various regions received practical training on public infrastructure projects, including schools and hospitals. This initiative aims to strengthen the ESCO market by improving the quality and reliability of energy efficiency assessments.
contextoradditionalinfo: The training is part of the 'Energy Audits — Unlocking the Energy Efficiency Potential of Public Buildings' project, implemented under the Public and Private Financing for Development (PPFD) program. It addresses the need for skilled professionals to support the development of Uzbekistan's ESCO market, which requires both a regulatory framework and technically sound project preparation to attract investment and reduce energy consumption in public buildings.
beneficiaries: energy auditors, private-sector representatives, government organizations
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification signed SAR40 million in contracts with Morooj National Foundation for sustainable forest management projects, marking the first national initiative of its kind to strengthen forest sustainability and preserve their environmental, economic, and social value while increasing the contribution of the non-profit sector to national environmental goals. The initiative uses GIS and remote sensing to assess forest conditions, including topography, degradation, and climate factors, and covers six areas: improving forest health, preventing and restoring fire-affected forests, rehabilitating degraded forests, engaging stakeholders and encouraging investment, strengthening forest monitoring, and assessing risks and developing mitigation measures.
decision_making_institution: The National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources (MAFWR) imposed a nationwide seasonal ban on the fishing, possession, transportation, sale, purchase, storage and trade of kingfish (kanad) along Oman’s coasts from 15 August to 15 October 2026. The measure, issued under the Marine Fisheries Law and Ministerial Decision No. 70/2026, aims to protect kingfish stocks during a critical stage of their life cycle and support the long-term sustainability of Oman’s fisheries and marine biodiversity. Fishermen and businesses holding existing stocks are required to register them with the relevant authorities, while violations are subject to legal penalties.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: The Malian government has announced the creation of a specialized center dedicated to land matters to resolve long-standing disputes in the sector. This centralized structure is designed to harmonize contradictory administrative procedures that have historically paralyzed land management. Additionally, the government ratified a financing agreement to improve electricity supply in Bamako to support businesses and households. A new National Citizen Mobilization Strategy was also approved to foster national belonging through civic education and cultural promotion.
contextoradditionalinfo: Mali is currently facing multiple security and economic challenges that have impacted the daily lives of its citizens. The land sector has been particularly affected by disputes that hindered development, while frequent power cuts in the capital have penalized the economy. These measures are part of a broader strategic effort by the government to stabilize the country and respond to both immediate emergencies and long-term development needs.
beneficiaries: the malian population, the société énergie, in the face, years, succès masra

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources has intensified seafood safety checks following a ship grounding near Al Qibliyah Island. The Food Safety and Quality Centre is actively conducting inspections and collecting samples of fish products from local markets to ensure compliance with health standards. Fishermen have been advised to avoid fishing in affected areas and to report any signs of environmental contamination. These measures are precautionary and intended to safeguard public health and the integrity of the local fish supply. The ministry continues to monitor the marine environment for potential impacts from the incident.
contextoradditionalinfo: A ship grounded near Al Qibliyah Island in the Al Hallaniyat Islands, Dhofar Governorate, raising concerns about potential marine pollution and its impact on seafood safety. The government initiated these monitoring and inspection activities as a precautionary measure to prevent contaminated fish from entering the food supply.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Argentina has ended the provision of free healthcare for foreign visitors and non-permanent residents at national hospitals. Foreign nationals without permanent residency or citizenship will now be billed directly for medical services or required to use their private health insurance. The policy specifically targets national-level institutions, though local governments retain the authority to implement similar measures. Emergency medical care remains exempt from billing to ensure immediate life-saving treatment is not delayed.
contextoradditionalinfo: Historically, Argentina provided universal basic services, including free healthcare, to all individuals regardless of their legal status. This policy shift marks a departure from that tradition, aiming to restrict public health resources to citizens and permanent residents while requiring others to cover their own medical costs.

policydecision_details: The Malta Food Safety Authority has issued a formal public warning regarding the presence of excessive tropane alkaloids in Salati Preziosi Pop Corn. The affected product is sold in 90g packs, specifically identified by lot number L26269 and a best before date of 16 December 2026. Consumers are strictly advised not to consume the product and are instructed to either dispose of it or return it to the point of purchase. This measure is taken under Chapter 649 of the Food Safety and Security Act to protect public health.
contextoradditionalinfo: The warning was triggered by information received from the product operator indicating that the popcorn contains harmful levels of tropane alkaloids, such as atropine and scopolamine. These naturally occurring chemical compounds can cause severe, life-threatening anticholinergic effects if ingested. The authority is acting to prevent potential health hazards associated with the consumption of the contaminated batch.

policydecision_details: The Estonian government has decided to indefinitely extend the reduced operating hours for road and rail border checkpoints with Russia. Checkpoints will continue to operate on a 12-hour daily schedule, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. This measure aims to maintain border security, optimize staffing for customs enforcement, and respond to the current geopolitical climate. The decision follows a period of declining cross-border traffic and remains in effect until further notice.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was originally introduced earlier in 2026 to improve border security and staffing efficiency. It is set against the backdrop of broader EU-Russia relations, specifically influenced by Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine. The government maintains that the need for enhanced security and customs enforcement at the eastern border remains unchanged.

policydecision_details: The Republic of Moldova has ratified a EUR 150 million (USD 174 million) financing contract with the European Investment Bank to implement the Livada Moldovei II project. This initiative provides a credit line to support investments in the agricultural sector, including horticulture, viticulture, livestock, and aquaculture. The funding aims to modernize agri-food infrastructure, promote digitalization, and improve food safety standards. Additionally, a portion of the funds is allocated to public investments in research and education infrastructure to strengthen the sector's competitiveness.
contextoradditionalinfo: This project continues a partnership established in 2016 with the first stage of the Livada Moldovei project. It is designed to align Moldova's agricultural sector with European Union standards, support the EU accession process, and reduce rural poverty. The project is part of the Reform and Growth Mechanism for the Republic of Moldova, implemented through the Neighbourhood Investment Platform.
decision_making_institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova
beneficiaries: micro-enterprises, small and medium-sized enterprises, horticultural producers, viticultural producers, livestock farmers, aquaculture producers

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and the Arab American University signed a cooperation memorandum to strengthen collaboration in agricultural education, scientific research, training, and knowledge exchange, with the aim of aligning academic programmes and research with the needs of the agricultural sector. The partnership will focus on areas including food and water security, smart agriculture and irrigation, drought and soil management, and agri-food industries, while providing students with practical training opportunities and supporting capacity development among ministry staff. The ministry will also facilitate cooperation through its facilities, particularly the National Agricultural Research Centre, to translate research and education into practical applications that support farmers and sustainable agricultural development.

The Ministry of Agriculture received 400,000 doses of SAT1 foot-and-mouth disease vaccine, funded by the Palestinian government, to expand the national livestock vaccination and identification campaign and protect sheep and cattle from animal diseases. The vaccines will be distributed across the governorates according to needs and priorities, building on ongoing veterinary interventions in high-priority areas. The campaign aims to improve livestock health, reduce potential economic losses, support farmers, and strengthen animal production and national food security. The ministry is also preparing additional vaccination activities, including a campaign using brucellosis vaccines provided through FAO with Italian government funding.

The Government of Ecuador has officially launched the National Policy for the Reduction of Maternal and Neonatal Morbidity and Mortality, which will remain in effect until 2035. This strategic instrument aims to accelerate the reduction of avoidable maternal and neonatal deaths by strengthening health services and addressing access gaps. The policy focuses on providing comprehensive, continuous, and intercultural care for women during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period. Implementation will involve a multi-sectoral approach, including local governments, academia, and international cooperation, with a detailed implementation plan expected within 90 days.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was developed to address the need for improved maternal and neonatal health outcomes in Ecuador, supported by international organizations like PAHO/WHO, UNICEF, and UNFPA. It aligns with regional strategies to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality in the Americas. The initiative seeks to ensure that women and adolescents can exercise their reproductive rights and access quality health services to prevent obstetric emergencies.

policydecision_details: The Asian Development Bank has approved an emergency assistance loan of USD 50 million to the Maldives for the Energy Security Emergency Project. This project aims to finance critical fuel imports to ensure the continuity of essential services. These services include electricity generation, water supply, food and health logistics, inter-island transport, and waste management. The loan serves as a financial buffer to maintain these services amidst rising global fuel prices.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Maldives is heavily dependent on fuel imports, which power 94 percent of its electricity and essential desalination plants. Ongoing conflict in the Middle East has caused a significant surge in global fuel prices, increasing the cost of the country's monthly fuel imports by 132 percent. This economic pressure has limited the government's capacity to finance these imports independently, necessitating emergency external financial support.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Central African Republic has commissioned the first phase of a 65 MW solar power plant in Sakaï 2, funded by a 90 million USD investment from the Emirati group GSU. This initial phase currently injects 15 MW into the national energy network (ENERCA) to supply the 3rd and 9th districts of Bangui. The project aims to provide electricity to 300,000 homes by the end of 2026. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to diversify the national energy mix and reduce reliance on aging hydroelectric infrastructure.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Central African Republic faces a severe energy deficit, with only 16.8% of the population having access to electricity in 2024. The national grid is historically concentrated around Bangui and Boali, and aging hydroelectric installations have struggled to meet rising demand, leading to frequent power cuts. The government has set a target of 50% electricity access by 2030, necessitating rapid expansion of production capacity and distribution networks.
decision_making_institution: Government of the Central African Republic
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Republic of Moldova has approved the 2026–2030 Water and Sewerage Program to modernize national water supply and sanitation infrastructure. The program focuses on improving management efficiency through municipal cooperation and regionalization of services. It aims to provide safe water access to at least 95% of the population and sewer system access to at least 65%. The initiative includes strengthening regulatory frameworks and implementing wastewater treatment requirements aligned with EU standards.
contextoradditionalinfo: The program was developed to address the need for sustainable and high-quality water and sanitation services, particularly in rural areas. It seeks to modernize aging infrastructure and ensure compliance with international environmental standards and European Union legislation.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure
beneficiaries: rural households, local authorities, service operators

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Government of the Republic of Moldova has approved the National Program for Reducing Natural Disaster Risks for 2026-2030. The program aims to modernize early warning systems, map vulnerable areas, and protect natural resources to mitigate the impact of extreme weather. Key measures include the creation of a national spatial data system, improved monitoring of meteorological phenomena, and the promotion of drought-adapted agricultural practices. The initiative seeks to proactively address climate risks before they result in significant economic and social losses.
decision_making_institution: Government of the Republic of Moldova
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, in cooperation with the Palestinian Hydrologists Group, established a 50-kilowatt solar energy unit in Firasin Village Council, funded through a Dutch-supported project. The initiative aims to reduce the cost of agricultural water pumping, improve farmers’ access to irrigation water, and provide a sustainable energy source for agricultural production. The project forms part of the Ministry’s efforts to improve agricultural infrastructure, promote renewable energy, reduce production costs, improve resource-use efficiency, and strengthen farmers’ resilience and ability to continue investing in their land.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture distributed 12 plastic water tanks to farming households in the Al-Masoudiya area through the Burqa Village Council under its rapid response programme. The intervention aims to provide farmers with essential water supplies, reduce the challenges they face, and strengthen their ability to continue cultivating and investing in their agricultural land. The support is part of the Ministry’s efforts to target agricultural assistance to areas most in need, strengthen farmers’ resilience, and sustain agricultural production.

The Malian transitional authorities have launched a 12.7 billion FCFA (USD 22.5 million) emergency plan to address rising food insecurity affecting 1.5 million people. The strategy includes the free distribution of 20,000 tonnes of cereals and a 50% subsidized sales system for essential staples like rice, millet, and oil. Additionally, the plan provides support for the local economy through the distribution of fish and livestock feed. This initiative, managed by the Food Safety Commission, aims to mitigate the impact of the lean season and projected food insecurity for 4 million Malians by the end of 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: Mali is facing a critical lean season with projections indicating that up to 4 million people could face food insecurity by the end of 2026. The country remains structurally dependent on external food aid, and the current plan is supported by international partners including Russia and China to address immediate humanitarian needs while attempting to bypass price-inflating intermediaries.

policydecision_details: The Lebanese parliament has passed a law to abolish the death penalty, becoming the first country in the Middle East to do so. The legislation replaces capital punishment with life imprisonment accompanied by aggravated hard labour. This decision follows a long-standing unofficial moratorium on executions that had been in place since 2004. The move aims to align the country's legal framework with global human rights trends.
contextoradditionalinfo: Lebanon had observed an unofficial moratorium on executions for over two decades, yet courts continued to issue death sentences. At the end of 2025, 85 individuals were on death row. The abolition of the death penalty occurs alongside ongoing parliamentary debates regarding a controversial general amnesty law.

policydecision_details: The European Commission has authorized the sixth disbursement of €6.234 billion to Spain under the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan. This payment, consisting of €4.962 billion (USD 5.7 billion) in grants and €1.008 billion (USD 1.17 billion) in loans, follows the successful completion of milestones and targets. The funds are intended to support ongoing reforms and investments in areas such as sustainable mobility, housing, social protection, and digital transformation. This disbursement brings the total received by Spain to €78 billion, representing 76.5% of the total allocated funds.
contextoradditionalinfo: The disbursement is part of the Recovery and Resilience Facility, which aims to support the economic, social, and territorial transformation of Spain following the COVID-19 pandemic. Spain has met 338 milestones and targets to date, demonstrating a commitment to structural reforms and effective investment implementation. The country is currently in the final phase of the plan, with preparations underway for the seventh and final payment application.
beneficiaries: the seventh and, implementing the plan, the country, more information see

policydecision_details: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to convert 30,000 metric tonnes of paddy held by the Paddy Marketing Board into rice. This rice will be processed by registered millers and released to the market through Lanka Sathosa and other retail outlets. A specialized Price Committee will determine the conversion ratio and the final selling price for consumers. The initiative aims to support the government's paddy purchasing programme while simultaneously increasing the availability of rice in the market.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision follows a recommendation from the Food Policy and Security Committee to address market supply concerns. By converting government-held paddy stocks into rice, the government intends to stabilize market supply and ensure that rice remains accessible to the public.

policydecision_details: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved Rs. 1.0675 billion (USD 3.3 million) in equity capital for Lanka Metro Transit (Private) Limited to expand urban public transport operations. The funding will be allocated over two years, with Rs. 800 million in 2026 for infrastructure development and Rs. 267.5 million in 2027 for operational activities. The investment supports the expansion of the fleet with 112 additional low-floor buses. Key infrastructure projects include a central workshop in Ekala and new bus depots in Thalangama, Kadawatha, Ratmalana, and Homagama.
contextoradditionalinfo: Lanka Metro Transit was incorporated in October 2025 to modernize public transportation in Sri Lanka. The company's pilot service in Colombo, utilizing buses from the Clean Sri Lanka programme, has demonstrated commercial viability and public acceptance, necessitating further investment to scale operations and infrastructure.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Hîncești District Council and the Galați County Council have launched a cross-border project titled 'Natural Disaster Prevention' with a total budget of over EUR 1.5 million (USD 1.7 million). The initiative focuses on strengthening the capacity of local authorities and communities to manage climate-related emergencies through the purchase of specialized equipment and the installation of early warning systems. Specifically, the project includes the acquisition of a multifunctional road maintenance vehicle for Galați County and a special emergency response vehicle for the Hîncești district.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project was initiated to address the increasing risks posed by climate-related events and emergencies in the border region between Moldova and Romania. By improving infrastructure, monitoring capabilities, and cross-border cooperation, the authorities aim to enhance the resilience of local communities against natural disasters.
decision_making_institution: Hîncești District Council and Galați County Council
beneficiaries: local authorities, communities in Galați County, communities in Hîncești District
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Tubas and Northern Jordan Valley Directorate of Agriculture, in coordination with the Palestinian Hydrologists Group, distributed pressure-controlled irrigation sub-networks, main transmission lines, and related equipment to 23 farmers in several areas of Tubas Governorate. The intervention is part of the Water, Land, and Agricultural Roads Investment Program, funded by the Dutch government and managed by the Welfare Association in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture. The project aims to improve irrigation efficiency, reduce water losses, increase water and land productivity, and strengthen agricultural infrastructure, helping farmers make better use of limited water resources and sustain investment in their agricultural land.

The Jenin Governorate Agriculture Directorate, in cooperation with the Palestinian Center for Economic and Social Development (ESDC), distributed 2,275 almond saplings to 10 small farmers across several communities in Jenin Governorate. The intervention is part of a project aimed at improving livelihoods, strengthening small farmers’ resilience, and promoting sustainable agriculture under changing circumstances. The initiative supports the productive use and preservation of agricultural land, provides new income and production opportunities for farming families, and strengthens farmers’ ability to maintain and invest in their land, particularly in areas vulnerable to land confiscation or seizure.

The Food Safety Department of Qatar's Ministry of Public Health intensified its monitoring activities during the second quarter of 2026. This involved inspecting 29,147 imported food shipments and conducting 5,748 inspection visits to local food establishments. The department also performed 136,280 laboratory tests to ensure compliance with national food safety standards. Additionally, the department expanded its digital services through the Watheq system to streamline food safety approvals.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of the Ministry's ongoing efforts to strengthen Qatar’s national food safety system and foster a culture of food safety among food establishments, workers, and the wider community. The increase in monitoring activities reflects a strategic focus on ensuring that all food products, whether imported or locally produced, meet established health and hygiene regulations.

policydecision_details: The Azores government has approved new management plans for protected terrestrial areas across six islands: Corvo, Flores, Graciosa, Santa Maria, São Jorge, and Terceira. These plans establish a regulatory framework for land use, zoning, and conservation objectives within the archipelago's Natural Parks. The initiative aims to balance environmental protection with sustainable human activities, including tourism. It also introduces monitoring programs to assess ecosystem health and mitigate environmental threats. This move represents a shift toward a more science-based environmental policy for the region.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of the Azores Regional Network of Protected Areas, which covers approximately 25% of the archipelago's territory. The government identified a need to update management instruments to better address climate change, natural hazards, and the pressure of tourism on sensitive ecosystems. By integrating conservation with sustainable use, the authorities aim to ensure the long-term resilience of the islands' biodiversity and geological heritage.
decision_making_institution: Regional Government Council of the Azores

policydecision_details: The Portuguese government has updated the legal regime for the Iberian wolf to improve the compensation system for livestock damages. Key changes include the elimination of progressive reductions in compensation values and the inclusion of compensation for animals that disappear following attacks. Additionally, the automatic exclusion of compensation for animals under one month old has been removed. These measures aim to ensure a fairer, more predictable system that supports the sustainability of agricultural farms while maintaining biodiversity conservation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address the conflict between the conservation of the protected Iberian wolf species and the economic viability of livestock farming in affected territories. By adjusting compensation criteria to better reflect real-world farming conditions, the government seeks to foster better coexistence between rural economic activities and environmental protection.

policydecision_details: The Minister of Territorial Planning, Urban Planning and Housing announced a temporary suspension of all new land allocations within the State domain in N’Djamena. This measure halts automatic land grants to ministerial departments and public institutions to address land pressure and speculation. Future allocations will be restricted to projects of major public interest, subject to rigorous feasibility studies and compliance checks. The policy aims to restore state authority over land management and protect reserves for future public investment. This initiative is part of a broader effort to modernize land administration and digitize procedures.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Territorial Planning, Urban Planning and Housing
beneficiaries: public institutions, local authorities, state bodies

policydecision_details: The Somali federal government has launched a USD 20 million road infrastructure project in Hargeisa as part of the broader Nagaad Project. This initial phase covers 23 kilometers of road and includes the construction of the Bundaweyn bridge. The project is part of a national strategy to improve economic infrastructure and connectivity across Somalia's federal member states. The Ministry of Public Works is overseeing the implementation of this and other road projects totaling 89 kilometers nationwide.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is supported by the World Bank and other international partners to enhance infrastructure and connectivity. It is being implemented amidst a long-standing political dispute between the Somali federal government and Somaliland, which declared independence in 1991 but lacks broad international recognition.
beneficiaries: the nagaad project, a major road

policydecision_details: The government of Kazakhstan has approved an updated master plan for Astana to guide urban development through 2035. The plan aims to accommodate a projected population increase to nearly 2.3 million residents. It outlines strategies for expanding housing, schools, transport networks, and essential utilities. The policy also establishes frameworks for land-use, environmental protection, and emergency resilience to support the city's rapid growth.
contextoradditionalinfo: Astana has experienced significant population growth since becoming the capital in 1997, with the number of residents increasing fivefold. The city currently faces pressure on infrastructure, housing, and social services due to sustained internal migration and natural growth. The updated master plan is designed to manage this expansion and ensure the city's long-term functional and environmental sustainability.

policy_description: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture – Northern Borders Region Branch launched the Farmers’ Market Festival to support local farmers and productive families by promoting the direct marketing and sale of locally produced agricultural and rural products. The festival showcases dates, vegetables, fruits, honey, and other food products, while also providing awareness activities on sustainable agricultural practices and encouraging consumption of national products. The initiative aims to increase the economic value of local production, support farmers’ livelihoods, and contribute to agricultural development and food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture
policycategory: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets

policydecision_details: The Somali Cabinet has approved a new Rules of Origin Law to establish a legal framework for issuing Certificates of Origin. This legislation enables Somali exporters to qualify for preferential tariff treatment under regional and continental trade agreements, such as the AfCFTA and the EAC. By certifying the origin of goods, the law aims to improve the competitiveness of Somali-made products in international markets. The government intends for this measure to stimulate domestic industries, attract investment, and reduce reliance on imports.
contextoradditionalinfo: Following Somalia's accession to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and membership in the East African Community (EAC), the government is implementing trade reforms to integrate into regional markets.
