The policy is part of a broader strategy to diversify the economy, increase export capacity, and support local manufacturing and agricultural bases.
beneficiaries: Somali exporters, Somali manufacturers, local businesses

policy_description: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture supports the development of the dates sector through seasonal events such as the Al-Khabra and Riyadh Al-Khabra Dates Festival, which stimulates date trading, strengthens logistics and supply chains, and creates seasonal employment opportunities. The festival also promotes local agricultural products, tourism, and economic activity in Qassim Region, while supporting the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030 through agricultural development, income diversification, increased local content, and improved competitiveness and sustainability of the dates sector.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture
policycategory: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Maritime Fisheries has finalized an amended version of Tunisia’s draft Water Code, incorporating observations from relevant ministries and institutions, and is preparing to submit it to the Council of Ministers before forwarding it to the Assembly of the Representatives of the People for consideration and adoption. The revised text includes draft implementing regulations and an explanatory note, with the proposed reforms aimed at strengthening Tunisia’s water governance framework and addressing the country’s water resource challenges. The draft has been under review for several years, and its advancement to the next legislative stage represents a step toward updating the national framework for water resources management.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Maritime Fisheries

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: The President of the United States has issued a proclamation to adjust imports of polysilicon and its derivatives to protect national security. The policy establishes a Minimum Import Price (MIP) program for these goods to ensure a commercially viable domestic market. Additionally, a 15 percent ad valorem duty is imposed on imports of downstream polysilicon derivatives. The Secretary of Commerce is authorized to enter into company-specific deals to incentivize domestic production and supply chain strengthening. These measures are designed to revitalize the U.S. polysilicon sector and reduce dependence on foreign imports.
contextoradditionalinfo: The U.S. polysilicon sector has faced significant decline due to global oversupply and foreign government policies, with the U.S. share of global production capacity falling from 50 percent in 2005 to less than 2 percent in 2024. Polysilicon is identified as a critical material for semiconductors and solar products, which are essential for national defense and modern economic infrastructure. The Secretary of Commerce determined that current import levels threaten national security by eroding domestic production capacity. This proclamation follows an investigation under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962.
beneficiaries: United States polysilicon producers, semiconductor manufacturers, solar energy industry
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Morocco has signed a concession agreement to develop a $1.5 billion waste-to-energy facility in Casablanca. The project aims to treat 1.5 million tonnes of municipal waste annually, significantly reducing reliance on landfills. It will generate approximately 126 megawatts of baseload electricity, supported by solar and biogas installations. This initiative is designed to boost renewable energy capacity and improve waste management infrastructure for over 4.2 million residents.
contextoradditionalinfo: Morocco is facing a growing electricity demand, estimated to rise by 3% annually through 2030. The project addresses the need for sustainable waste management and supports the country's broader energy transition goals by shifting away from methane-emitting landfill practices.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Moroccan government has unveiled a MAD 15 billion (USD 1.65 billion) expansion of its national employment strategy under the Employment Roadmap 2030. This initiative aims to accelerate job creation and improve labor market access for young people, including those who are not in education, employment, or training. The plan expands existing employment programs to include non-graduates and strengthens the role of the National Agency for the Promotion of Employment and Skills (ANAPEC). It also incorporates a localized approach by conducting regional labor market assessments to tailor programs to specific economic conditions.
beneficiaries: youth, non-graduate youth, women, entrepreneurs, small businesses

policydecision_details: The WWF North Africa has launched a marine waste recycling initiative in Tunisia’s Gulf of Gabès to remove abandoned fishing gear, reduce marine pollution, and support the circular economy. Through an integrated waste management system, recovered materials are sorted for reuse by artisan cooperatives or recycled by licensed companies, while non-recyclable waste is safely disposed of through approved facilities. The initiative also strengthens the capacities of fishermen’s groups and local organizations, promotes sustainable livelihoods, restores coastal ecosystems, and supports blue carbon mechanisms by protecting Posidonia oceanica seagrass meadows to enhance climate resilience.

The Japanese Cabinet has approved a plan to reduce the consumption tax rate on food and beverages from 8 percent to 1 percent for a two-year period starting in April 2027. This measure is designed to provide inflation relief to households and will be accompanied by cash handouts for low- and middle-income earners to ensure an effectively zero tax burden. The government intends to fund this initiative through budgetary reforms rather than deficit-covering bonds. Additionally, the government plans to provide support to small farmers and restaurant operators who may be negatively impacted by the tax reduction.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to persistent inflation affecting Japanese households. It fulfills a campaign pledge made by the ruling Liberal Democratic Party and its coalition partners to reduce the tax burden on essential goods. The decision follows deliberations by a national council on taxation and social security, which determined that a full zero-percent tax rate was not immediately feasible due to technical constraints in retail cash register systems.
beneficiaries: low-income earners, middle-income earners, small farmers, restaurant operators
commodity1: Meat and other animal derived products

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the Palestinian Center for Economic and Social Development (ESDC), Agricultural Relief, and other partners, distributed 4,000 irrigated almond and apricot saplings to 25 farmers in the Tubas and Northern Jordan Valley Governorate. The initiative aims to increase investment in agricultural land, expand orchard cultivation, improve agricultural production, enhance the efficient use of natural resources, strengthen farmers’ resilience, and support food security and sustainable agricultural development. The project is funded by the Dutch Representative Office as part of broader efforts to improve livelihoods and promote sustainable economic growth in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

The Namibian Cabinet has approved the National Upstream Petroleum Local Content Policy to maximize local participation in the petroleum sector. The policy focuses on employment creation, local procurement, enterprise development, and technology transfer. It aims to ensure that Namibians have increased ownership and participation across the entire petroleum value chain. This framework is designed to foster industrialization and sustainable economic development within the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to ensure that the country's emerging petroleum sector contributes directly to national development goals. By mandating local content, the government seeks to prevent the exclusion of local businesses and workers from the benefits of natural resource extraction. This aligns with broader national efforts to strengthen industrialization and local value addition.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Kazakhstan has signed an agreement to develop a nationwide flood and drought early warning system to shift from reactive emergency response to proactive anticipation. The project integrates hydrological data with water infrastructure information into a unified forecasting system. This initiative is part of the broader Water Partnership Initiative 2024–2030, which aims to modernize water management through digital tools and innovation. The system will provide authorities with improved decision-making capabilities to mitigate risks associated with climate variability.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to increasing pressure from climate change, recurring droughts and floods, and the growing demand for water resources in Kazakhstan. The government recognizes the need to modernize aging infrastructure and transition toward a new model of water management that prioritizes conservation and digital integration. This effort is supported by international development partners and private-sector collaboration to enhance national preparedness.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and the Palestinian Center for Economic and Social Development distributed almond saplings to farmers in the Farasin area under a project to improve livelihoods and strengthen the resilience of small farmers. The initiative aims to encourage the cultivation and protection of agricultural land, expand almond production, improve farmers' incomes, enhance food security, and support sustainable agricultural development while helping farmers maintain agricultural activities in threatened areas.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The General Directorate of Meteorology (DGM) issued an orange heatwave alert for several provinces in Morocco, warning of El Niño-induced extremely high temperatures that could affect agricultural production. The heatwave is expected to increase crop water requirements, intensify heat stress on crops, and raise water losses through evaporation, while also posing risks to livestock health. Farmers are advised to optimize irrigation schedules, monitor irrigation systems, ensure adequate water and shade for livestock, and minimize animal handling during peak heat periods to reduce the impacts on agricultural productivity.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation, in partnership with the Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority (ASEZA) and with technical support from the U.S. Government, launched a single-window digital platform for the National Water Carrier Project to streamline licensing and permit procedures through a unified online system. The platform enhances coordination among government institutions, accelerates project implementation, improves transparency and administrative efficiency, and supports Jordan’s water security by facilitating the delivery of one of the country’s key strategic water infrastructure projects through digital integration and governance reforms.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation

policydecision_details: The Nama Water Services, in partnership with Hema Energy, launched a pilot project to cultivate Camelina using recycled water to promote sustainable agriculture, biofuel production, and the circular use of treated wastewater. Supported by Sultan Qaboos University, the Environment Authority, and the Oman Net Zero Centre, the initiative will assess Camelina’s carbon sequestration potential and commercial viability while contributing to water security, reducing carbon emissions, and advancing Oman’s green economy and clean energy transition.

Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have strengthened bilateral trade and transport cooperation through a digital customs linkage and ongoing railway collaboration to improve cross-border logistics and regional connectivity. The new customs system enables the secure, real-time exchange of customs data before shipments reach border crossings, accelerating clearance procedures, reducing administrative barriers, improving risk management, and facilitating trade flows. The two countries are also advancing railway cooperation and sharing technical expertise to enhance transport infrastructure and support long-term economic integration across the Gulf region.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), in partnership with the International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) and the Ministry of Water Resources, with funding from Global Affairs Canada (GAC), launched the MURUNA project to strengthen Iraq’s resilience to water scarcity and climate change. The initiative will improve water governance, enhance community-level water management, rehabilitate water infrastructure, and promote climate-smart agriculture to help vulnerable farming communities adapt to drought, desertification, rising temperatures, and declining river flows, while supporting long-term food security and sustainable agricultural development.
decision_making_institution: The International Center for Biosaline Agriculture (ICBA) and the Ministry of Water Resources
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture, through the Jenin Directorate of Agriculture, in partnership with the Palestinian Center for Economic and Social Development (ESDC), distributed almond saplings to small farmers to expand fruit tree cultivation, improve land productivity, and strengthen sustainable livelihoods. The initiative supports the resilience of small farmers by promoting sustainable agricultural production, encouraging investment in agricultural land, enhancing food security, and improving farmers' ability to cope with ongoing challenges.

The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the Palestinian Hydrologists Group and with funding from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) through the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ), launched a project to strengthen the resilience of small farmers by distributing pressurized irrigation equipment in Tulkarm Governorate. The initiative promotes modern irrigation technologies to improve water-use efficiency, conserve water resources, increase agricultural productivity, enhance climate resilience, and support sustainable agricultural production and food security.

The Ministry of Agriculture, in partnership with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and supported by the IBSA Fund (Governments of India, Brazil, and South Africa), signed an agreement to establish and equip an alternative animal feed production unit in Bardala. The project will convert agricultural waste into livestock feed, benefiting local livestock breeders by reducing production costs, improving resource efficiency, strengthening the sustainability of the livestock sector, and enhancing farmers' resilience through training and modern feed production technologies

The Government of Iraq and the Government of Türkiye are implementing a bilateral water cooperation agreement that has significantly increased upstream water flows in the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, while introducing an oil-for-water financing mechanism to support water infrastructure projects through joint Iraqi–Turkish implementation. The agreement establishes a framework for coordinated seasonal water releases based on Iraq’s needs, aiming to improve long-term water security. The initiative comes as Iraq continues to face water scarcity driven by upstream dam development, climate change, El Niño-induced declining rainfall, and resource management challenges, although recent abundant rainfall has temporarily improved reservoir levels.

Somalia has officially launched new regulations governing the marketing of breast-milk substitutes to align with international standards. The policy aims to protect breastfeeding practices by limiting inappropriate commercial influence on infant-feeding choices. Developed in collaboration with UNICEF and WHO, the regulations seek to improve maternal and child health outcomes. The government intends to enforce these rules through monitoring and stronger support services for breastfeeding mothers.
contextoradditionalinfo: Exclusive breastfeeding rates in Somalia remain significantly below recommended levels, with only 34% of infants under six months being exclusively breastfed. The government introduced these regulations to address this gap and ensure that breastfeeding remains a viable and protected option for families. The launch was timed to coincide with World Breastfeeding Week to emphasize the importance of breastfeeding for child survival and development.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Health and Human Services

policydecision_details: The Republic of Moldova approved over 82 million lei (USD 17 million) in subsidies for August 2026 to support the agricultural sector. A significant portion, 50 million lei, was allocated as state financial aid to 333 producers affected by the 2025 drought. Additionally, 22.30 million lei was directed to the LEADER rural development programme for community and business projects. Further funds were provided as post-investment subsidies for agri-food applications and advance payments for livestock farms.
contextoradditionalinfo: The funding package addresses the lingering economic impact of the 2025 drought on agricultural producers and supports ongoing rural development and investment in the agri-food sector.
decision_making_institution: AIPA (Agency for Intervention and Payments for Agriculture)
beneficiaries: agricultural producers, livestock farmers, rural communities

policydecision_details: China has activated minimum purchase price programs for wheat and early-season indica rice to support farmers and stabilize market expectations. The policy involves government-led grain purchases in key producing provinces like Jiangxi, Hunan, and Henan. Authorities are combining these market-based purchases with the management of national grain reserves. Additionally, the government is strengthening local infrastructure for grain drying and storage to reduce post-harvest losses. These measures aim to ensure that farmers can sell their crops smoothly during the peak harvest season.
contextoradditionalinfo: As China's summer grain purchases reach their peak, the government is intervening to protect farmers' interests against potential price volatility. By setting a policy floor for grain prices, the administration seeks to maintain market stability and ensure consistent supply chains between grain-producing and consuming regions.
decision_making_institution: National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration

policydecision_details: Somali President has signed the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement into law following parliamentary ratification. This action completes the domestic approval process, allowing Somalia to deposit its instrument of ratification with the African Union Commission. The government aims to integrate the country into the African single market to foster economic diversification and industrialization. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry will now begin implementing the agreement by aligning tariff schedules and preparing local traders for regional competition.
contextoradditionalinfo: Somalia has been pursuing closer regional economic integration as part of broader economic reforms aimed at expanding trade, attracting investment, and strengthening the private sector. Membership in the AfCFTA is intended to provide preferential access to a market of over 1.4 billion people, thereby creating new opportunities for exports and job creation.
beneficiaries: Somali businesses, manufacturers, cooperatives, investors, exporters, small and medium-sized enterprises

policydecision_details: Somalia has officially launched the Somali Surgical Society to enhance surgical care and professional standards across the country. The association aims to unite surgeons from various specialties to foster collaboration, research, and continuing professional development. This initiative is designed to support the implementation of the National Surgical, Obstetric, Trauma and Anaesthesia Strategic Plan. Furthermore, the society will facilitate efforts to join the College of Surgeons of East, Central and Southern Africa (COSECSA) to improve training and international recognition for the surgical workforce.
contextoradditionalinfo: The establishment of the Somali Surgical Society serves as a cornerstone for developing the country's surgical workforce and addressing gaps in specialist training. By creating an organized professional body, the government intends to improve the quality of surgical services and align national training programs with regional standards set by COSECSA.

policydecision_details: The Government of Kenya and UK institutions have signed a five-year memorandum of understanding to deepen health ties. This agreement builds on a previous partnership to enhance health workforce development and specialist clinical services. The new framework expands the scope to include digital health, artificial intelligence, and local manufacturing of health products. It also aligns health programs with Kenya's national health policy to improve coordination and sustainability.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreement serves to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Kenya and the UK, aiming to accelerate innovation, research, and investment in the health sector. It is designed to support the rollout of Kenya's Universal Health Coverage agenda and build more resilient, climate-resilient health systems.

policydecision_details: The Cambodian Senate unanimously approved four bills to enhance trade and economic integration with ASEAN and international markets. These measures include accession to the Convention on International Interests in Mobile Equipment and its Aircraft Protocol to improve aviation financing. Additionally, the Senate approved three ASEAN Mutual Recognition Arrangements covering product certification, construction materials, and automotive type approvals. These agreements aim to harmonize standards, facilitate the movement of goods, and reduce compliance costs for businesses. The legislative package is designed to align Cambodia's regulatory framework with regional standards.
contextoradditionalinfo: Cambodia is seeking to strengthen its economic integration within the ASEAN bloc and the broader international market. By adopting international conventions and harmonizing technical standards, the government aims to increase investor confidence, facilitate trade, and improve the competitiveness of its domestic industries in sectors such as aviation, construction, and automotive manufacturing.
beneficiaries: aviation companies, construction material producers, automotive manufacturers

policydecision_details: Launched the second phase of capital raising for the construction of the Bujumbura Central Market (BUJA CITY PLAZA). This public-private partnership aims to finance the first construction phase of a modern commercial complex on the site of the former central market. The project involves issuing investment units to domestic and international investors to support infrastructure development. The investment model is designed to span 24 years, after which ownership will be transferred to the Burundian government.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is part of a broader strategy to leverage Burundi's capital market to attract investment for critical infrastructure development. By replacing the old central market with a modern facility, the government aims to stimulate economic growth and improve commercial infrastructure. The project is governed by a concession agreement and approved under the national Public-Private Partnership (PPP) framework.

policydecision_details: The telecommunications administrations of Tajikistan and Uzbekistan conducted joint technical measurements to ensure electromagnetic compatibility of radio electronic equipment in border areas. The initiative involved radio monitoring, information exchange, and network optimization to minimize signal interference. As a result, 16 base stations were adjusted by reassigning a television broadcasting channel to restore service quality. These measures aim to improve the reliability of mobile, television, and radio communication services for residents in border districts.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy addresses the challenge of minimizing unwanted radio signal propagation and mutual interference in border areas between Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. By fostering bilateral cooperation, the administrations seek to ensure the efficient use of the radio frequency spectrum and enhance the quality of telecommunications infrastructure for citizens living in border regions.
decision_making_institution: Communications Service under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan

policydecision_details: The Government of Lesotho has mandated that all wool and mohair stakeholders must adhere to new, strict biosecurity measures. This decision follows a recent outbreak of Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) in the country. Compliance is required to ensure the continued competitiveness of Lesotho's products in the global mohair industry. Stakeholders are expected to implement these protocols immediately to mitigate further disease spread.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced as a direct response to a Foot and Mouth Disease outbreak, which poses a significant threat to the livestock sector and the international trade of wool and mohair products.

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Somalia and Türkiye are moving toward the implementation phase of a bilateral fisheries agreement. A Turkish delegation visited Mogadishu Port to assess infrastructure and conduct technical discussions regarding logistical support for fishing vessels. The agreement focuses on coordinating technical cooperation, investment, and operational planning for fish production, processing, and exports. Joint technical committees have been established to oversee the partnership's implementation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The fisheries agreement is part of a broader cooperation framework signed between Somalia and Türkiye in March 2024. Somalia aims to develop its fisheries industry as a key pillar of its blue economy to attract investment, create jobs, and better utilize its extensive marine resources.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (Türkiye) and Government of Somalia
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The government of Fiji has secured US$80 million in financing from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB). This funding is designated to enhance the nation's economic resilience and improve its preparedness for climate-related challenges. The investment aims to strengthen national infrastructure and institutional capacity to withstand external shocks. This financial support represents a strategic effort to ensure long-term stability for the country's economy.
contextoradditionalinfo: Fiji is highly vulnerable to climate change and economic volatility, necessitating external financial support to bolster its resilience and adaptive capacity. The AIIB financing is intended to address these systemic risks by providing the necessary capital for development and preparedness initiatives.
beneficiaries: the latest news, latest news on, independent news
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Government of Fiji has commissioned a new 10-kilometre farm road in the Macuata district to improve market access for over 200 farmers. The project, completed under the Rural Outer Island (ROI) Development Programme, cost USD 460,000. This infrastructure is designed to facilitate the transportation of agricultural produce to markets and improve access to essential farming supplies. The initiative aims to stimulate economic growth and support the livelihoods of rural communities in the Dogotuki, Udu, and Cikobia districts.
contextoradditionalinfo: Rural communities in Fiji often face challenges in accessing markets and essential services due to inadequate road infrastructure. The Rural Outer Island (ROI) Development Programme was established to address these infrastructure gaps, thereby connecting remote farming areas to the main road network and encouraging further agricultural investment.

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Health, Family and Welfare of the Maldives has issued the Regulation on the Responsibilities of Food Inspectors (2026/R-65). This regulation formalizes the duties and operational scope of food inspectors within the country. It aims to strengthen the oversight of food safety standards to protect public health. The regulation was officially dated and published on August 12, 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: This regulation is part of the ongoing efforts by the Maldivian government to enhance food safety governance and ensure that food inspection processes are clearly defined and legally binding.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Health, Family and Welfare

policydecision_details: The Sovereign Wealth Fund Act establishes a legal framework for the creation and management of a sovereign wealth fund. The act outlines the governance, investment objectives, and oversight mechanisms for the fund. It aims to manage national wealth for long-term economic stability and development.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to provide a structured mechanism for managing national financial resources, ensuring long-term fiscal sustainability and economic growth for the country.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Moldovan legislature has approved a bill to simplify administrative procedures for installing photovoltaic and energy storage systems. The legislation removes barriers that previously hindered the development of renewable energy generation capacity. It establishes a simplified authorization procedure for electricity storage facilities and specific residential solar installations. These measures aim to accelerate private and commercial investment in renewable energy infrastructure across various sectors.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address administrative bottlenecks that were slowing down the adoption of renewable energy technologies. By streamlining the regulatory framework, the government intends to facilitate the implementation of renewable energy projects and ensure that secondary regulations align with construction authorization standards. This initiative is part of a broader effort to modernize energy infrastructure and reduce legislative discrepancies.
decision_making_institution: Legislature of the Republic of Moldova
beneficiaries: residential building owners, commercial facility operators, agricultural facility operators, industrial facility operators
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Launched the second phase of the National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) programme, disbursing Sh3 billion to support youth-led small businesses. Each beneficiary receives a total of Sh50,000, split between a grant for business operations and a contribution to a savings scheme. The initiative aims to help young entrepreneurs scale their ventures into sustainable enterprises. Additionally, the government is introducing a national identification mechanism for beneficiaries and proposing a two-year business permit waiver to reduce operational costs.
contextoradditionalinfo: The NYOTA programme is part of Kenya's broader strategy to invest in youth enterprise and economic development. By providing direct financial support and reducing regulatory barriers, the government seeks to foster entrepreneurship and economic inclusion among the youth population across the country.

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: The Uzbekistan Institute of Standards approved the national standard O'z MSt 945:2026, titled 'Fishing Nets. Technical Conditions'. This standard establishes specific structural dimensions, strength requirements, and raw material specifications for nets used in commercial fishing. It aims to ensure that all fishing gear complies with operational and environmental regulations. The implementation is intended to protect aquatic biological resources and minimize adverse impacts on aquatic ecosystems.
contextoradditionalinfo: The standard was developed in execution of Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 80, dated 9 February 2024, which mandated the creation and approval of a national standard for nets permitted in commercial fishing. It is part of broader efforts to enhance ecological safety and strengthen the protection of aquatic resources in Uzbekistan.
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: The Minister of Agriculture, Rural Development and Food Production officially handed over agricultural equipment and inputs worth 2.8 billion CFA (USD 5 million) to producers in the Bagoué, Hambol, Poro, and Tchologo regions. The support includes improved seeds, insecticides, tractors, tillers, and combine harvesters to boost local food production. This initiative targets 360 professional agricultural organizations and nearly 6,000 producers, with a focus on women and youth. The goal is to modernize agriculture, reduce the arduousness of farm work, and increase the production of key food crops by an estimated 20,000 tonnes.
contextoradditionalinfo: This initiative is part of the Agro-industrial Pole Project in the North (2PAI-NORD) and the Food Sector Development Support Project (PADSV). It aligns with the government's vision to modernize Ivorian agriculture, improve productivity, and attract young people to the sector by providing mechanization and adapted financing.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Food Production
beneficiaries: professional agricultural organizations, producers, women, young people

policydecision_details: The Jordan Valley Authority has inaugurated a project to rehabilitate and expand the Al Hasa reservoir in the South Jordan Valley. Funded by the U.S. Embassy, the project aims to increase storage capacity, upgrade control and operation systems, and improve sedimentation and treatment facilities. These enhancements are designed to reduce water loss and improve irrigation efficiency for approximately 55,000 dunums of land. The initiative supports the national water sector strategy by ensuring a more reliable water supply for agriculture, industry, and local communities.
contextoradditionalinfo: Jordan is one of the most water-stressed regions in the world, facing significant challenges due to climate change and limited natural resources. The Al Hasa reservoir is a critical strategic facility that manages 24 million cubic meters of water annually. This rehabilitation project was initiated to address these water scarcity challenges and strengthen the resilience of the agricultural sector in the southern Jordan Valley.

policydecision_details: The Government of Lesotho has announced a subsidy program covering 70%-80% of the costs for seeds and fertilizers. This initiative is designed to directly support agricultural production across the country. The government emphasizes its commitment to integrity, efficiency, and honesty in the administration of these subsidies. The measure aims to lower input costs for farmers to boost overall agricultural output.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to boost agricultural production in Lesotho, likely addressing challenges related to input affordability and food security.

policy_description: Public/mutual fund and contingent risk financing
policydecision_details: The Government of Fiji has approved the 2026–2031 National Disaster Risk Financing Policy to enhance financial resilience against climate-related disasters. This policy aims to address the country's rising exposure to cyclones, floods, and other climate and geophysical hazards. It will guide national preparedness and improve financial planning for the government. Implementation will be led by the Ministry of Finance in collaboration with the National Disaster Risk Management Office, the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, and the Reserve Bank of Fiji.
contextoradditionalinfo: Fiji remains highly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change and frequent extreme weather events. The government identified disaster risk reduction and financing as a key priority to manage fiscal risks associated with these disasters. Currently, insurance coverage for households and businesses against disaster risks is low, estimated at only 12 percent.
policycategory: Public/mutual fund and contingent risk financing

policydecision_details: Energy and water ministers from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan signed a trilateral protocol in Tashkent to establish agreed water release volumes and schedules from the Toktogul Reservoir. This agreement ensures that water flows are regulated to support downstream irrigation needs for farmers in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan during the agricultural season. The protocol aims to provide certainty for agricultural activities and maintain water and energy stability across the region. The countries have committed to continued coordination, with a follow-up meeting planned for mid-June to finalize schedules for the summer months.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Toktogul Reservoir is critical for both electricity generation in Kyrgyzstan and irrigation for downstream agriculture in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. Historically, Kyrgyzstan's increased electricity generation during winter lowers reservoir levels, which can reduce water availability for spring and summer irrigation. This trilateral agreement builds upon previous winter cooperation, where Kazakhstan supplied electricity to Kyrgyzstan to help preserve water reserves in the reservoir for the current growing season.
decision_making_institution: Energy and Water Ministries of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan
beneficiaries: farmers in Kazakhstan, farmers in Uzbekistan

policydecision_details: China has implemented a zero-tariff policy for goods originating from Zimbabwe and 52 other African countries. This measure provides duty-free access to the Chinese market for a wide range of products, including agricultural commodities, processed foods, and manufactured goods. The policy aims to strengthen economic cooperation and facilitate market diversification for Zimbabwean exporters. It encourages a shift from raw commodity exports toward higher-value products to support industrialization.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy reflects China's growing appetite for African products and its strategic commitment to strengthening economic ties with the continent. For Zimbabwe, it serves as a critical opportunity to increase export volumes and move up the value chain, building on existing trade relationships in sectors like tobacco and minerals. The move is intended to help Zimbabwean firms overcome previous tariff barriers and improve their competitive position in the Chinese market.
commodity3: Others meat or animal derived products

policydecision_details: China has implemented a zero-tariff policy for imports originating from 53 African countries, including Egypt, effective May 1, 2026. This measure aims to boost Egyptian agricultural exports to the Chinese market by reducing market-entry costs. The policy is intended to foster a more integrated trade partnership, encouraging the transition from raw crop exports to value-added manufactured food products. It is expected to strengthen bilateral economic ties and support the development of industrial and logistics value chains.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a strategic effort by China to reshape its partnership with African nations on a more balanced basis amid global trade protectionism. It complements existing economic cooperation frameworks, such as the 2025 debt swap program for development, to enhance productive capacities in partner countries. Egyptian experts view this as a significant opportunity to increase the competitiveness of their agricultural sector and diversify their export portfolio.

policydecision_details: Issued the Income-tax (Third Amendment) Rules, 2026, which introduce a new Income Tax Return form (ITR-BN) specifically for block assessments. These rules apply to search and seizure cases initiated under section 247 or requisitions made under section 248 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. The amendment mandates the use of this new form for reporting income during the specified block period.
contextoradditionalinfo: This policy is part of the regulatory framework for tax administration in India, specifically addressing the procedural requirements for block assessments following search and seizure operations under the updated Income-tax Act of 2025.

policydecision_details: Ministerial Agreement No. 15 establishes the constitutional framework for the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries to promote food sovereignty. The policy mandates the state to support small and medium-sized production units through the promotion of agri-food transformation and the introduction of ecological technologies. It further commits to establishing preferential financing mechanisms to facilitate the acquisition of production means. This agreement serves as the administrative foundation for future specific programs aimed at strengthening national agricultural productivity and competitiveness.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is rooted in the Constitution of the Republic of Ecuador, specifically Articles 82, 85, 281, 284, and 285, which define food sovereignty as a strategic objective. The state is obligated to guarantee self-sufficiency in healthy and culturally appropriate food. This agreement aligns fiscal and economic policies with the constitutional mandate to redistribute income and provide public goods that ensure the rights of citizens and the sustainability of the agricultural sector.
decision_making_institution: Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries
beneficiaries: small and medium-sized production units, communities, social and solidarity economy actors

policy_description: Price control|Local production of fertilizers and other agricultural inputs
policydecision_details: Controlled fertiliser prices by directing companies to stockpile raw materials, diversify supply sources and optimize production.
policycategory: Price control|Local production of fertilizers and other agricultural inputs

policydecision_details: Authorities confirmed food supplies remain sufficient while inspection and clearance capacity was intensified due to higher import volumes linked to regional disruptions.
contextoradditionalinfo: MEC2026

policydecision_details: New shipping services and logistics corridors added to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, including alternative routes through Red Sea ports to secure food and essential commodity flows amid regional escalation.
contextoradditionalinfo: MEC2026

policydecision_details: Viet Nam has temporarily cut fuel taxes to zero, including environmental protection tax and value‑added tax (VAT), to stabilize domestic fuel prices amid global energy shocks linked to Middle East tensions. Under Prime Minister Decision No. 482/QD‑TTg, from 26 March to 15 April 2026, gasoline, diesel and aviation fuel face 0 VND environmental tax, exemption from VAT declaration and payment, and a 0 percent special consumption tax, with the government considering extending the measure through end‑June 2026 pending parliamentary approval.

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Maintained fuel subsidies to protect consumers from global price volatility. The state currently absorbs Rs. 100 (approximately USD 0.33) per litre of diesel and Rs. 20 (approximately USD 0.07) per litre of petrol. This results in a monthly expenditure of approximately Rs. 20 billion (USD 66.7 million). The government is also managing fuel imports through a scheduled tender process to ensure supply availability.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: Morocco and the United Kingdom formalized Decision No. 01/2026 to update the commercial framework of their bilateral Association Agreement. The decision amends Protocol 4, specifically revising the definition of originating products and administrative cooperation methods. It introduces updated cumulation rules that allow manufacturing processes in several countries to count as UK-origin content. Additionally, it clarifies direct transport rules and procedures for issuing certificates of origin to facilitate trade.
contextoradditionalinfo: The update aims to support the growing bilateral trade relationship, which reached $5.75 billion in 2024, and to accommodate the increasing scale and complexity of trade flows. Both nations seek to double bilateral trade and encourage investment in infrastructure, energy, and logistics sectors. This technical adjustment provides the necessary infrastructure to support these ambitious economic goals.
commodity2: Other products, not included in the other categories

policydecision_details: Tightened the fertiliser export regulations, intensifying volatility in the global fertiliser supply chain.

Launched a national informal settlements upgrading programme to improve living conditions in unplanned urban areas. The strategy focuses on in-situ upgrading, which includes regularizing land through proper spatial layout plans and plot demarcation. It also involves improving tenure security by issuing title deeds or 99-year leaseholds to residents. Furthermore, the government is implementing the incremental installation of basic infrastructure services such as roads, water, electricity, sanitation, and waste management. This initiative aims to integrate informal settlements into the formal urban system rather than pursuing displacement.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Housing and Urban Development

policydecision_details: Advanced purchasing agreements, a base price framework and the creation of a national corn commercialization system. The mesuares seek to mitigate the impact of falling international grain prices.
contextoradditionalinfo: MEC2026

policydecision_details: The Georgia Forestry Innovation Initiative (GFII) has announced an $8.9 million investment to foster innovation within the state's forestry sector. The initiative focuses on developing new technologies and identifying higher-value uses for low-value timber and mill residues. It aims to establish pilot facilities to transition research into commercial applications. The long-term objective is to support the creation of new manufacturing sites and strengthen the overall forest products industry.
contextoradditionalinfo: The investment is designed to expand the forestry industry through technological advancement and innovation. By creating new markets and opportunities for forest landowners to capture value from their resources, the initiative seeks to ensure the long-term economic viability of the sector. It addresses the need for evolving industry practices to remain competitive and sustainable.

Formally approved a standard dress code for all healthcare professionals and support staff working in hospitals and healthcare centers. This policy aims to ensure a unified professional appearance, improve hygiene standards, and enhance patient safety across the healthcare system. The standard provides structured options for uniforms, including formal wear and scrubs, to maintain consistency. It was developed by a Technical Working Group and approved by the High-Level Committee to address previous variations in staff attire.

On February 3, 2026, the Eurasian Economic Commission (EEC) Council approves duty exemption for Kyrgyzstan raw sugar imports as much as 20,000 tonnes, for Armernia as much as 20,000 tonnes and for Kazakhstan as much as 100,000 tonnes.

Kyrgyzstan unveils new Master Plan for 2050. The drafted law defines long-term priorities for the capital’s growth across several sectors. Once adopted, the plan will become the principal framework for territorial planning and will be legally binding for decisions related to construction and land use.

The Macao SAR Government has initiated the planning process for the Third Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development, covering the period from 2026 to 2030. This plan serves as a strategic roadmap for the region's development across various sectors, including administration and justice. An exchange session was held to discuss the specific objectives and policy directions within the administration and justice area. The plan aims to guide the region's socio-economic progress over the five-year term.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Five-Year Plan is a recurring strategic framework used by the Macao SAR Government to outline its long-term development goals and policy priorities. This specific session focuses on the administration and justice sector as part of the broader preparation for the 2026-2030 cycle.

policydecision_details: China has issued a comprehensive plan to strengthen its financial sector for the 2026-2030 period. The strategy focuses on preventing financial risks, enhancing financial supervision, and promoting high-quality development of the real economy. Key objectives include establishing a modern financial system with Chinese characteristics and improving the effectiveness of financial support for economic development. The plan also emphasizes capital market reforms and the optimization of the monetary policy framework to ensure long-term stability.
contextoradditionalinfo: The plan is part of China's broader economic strategy to transition from scale-driven expansion to quality-focused growth. It aims to address structural changes in the economy and ensure that the financial sector remains resilient against major risk events. By 2030, the government intends to have a robust legal and regulatory framework that supports international competitiveness and high-standard financial opening up.

policydecision_details: China has implemented a package of 16 targeted measures to modernize its tax system through the integration of advanced AI large models. The initiative focuses on streamlining tax and fee processing, enhancing digital service delivery, and providing proactive compliance guidance. Key features include intelligent assistants for automated tax filing, 24/7 AI-human hybrid support systems, and improved cross-departmental data sharing. These measures aim to reduce taxpayer waiting times, increase resolution rates, and shift from post-event supervision to early risk alerts.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of the 13th consecutive 'Spring Breeze Action to Facilitate Citizens' Handling of Tax Affairs', an annual campaign aimed at improving tax administration efficiency. The digital push seeks to simplify complex tax processes, such as annual reconciliations and VAT deductions, while fostering a more business-friendly environment through technology-driven service upgrades.
beneficiaries: taxpayers, fee payers, foreign-funded enterprises, flexible employment workers

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The State Council has approved a national plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-30) to expand consumption, marking the first time such a goal has been incorporated into a dedicated national plan. The policy targets total retail sales of consumer goods of around 60 trillion yuan by 2030 and aims to increase the contribution of consumption to GDP growth. Key measures include relaxing market-access restrictions in the services sector, promoting new business models driven by AI, and increasing public-service spending on education, healthcare, and eldercare. The plan also encourages financial institutions to expand lending for consumption and improve interest subsidies for personal and business loans.
contextoradditionalinfo: As China approaches high-income economy status with per capita GDP reaching approximately $14,000 in 2025, the country is experiencing a structural shift from goods-led consumption to services-led consumption. Despite this, China's household consumption rate remains relatively low compared to other major economies, suggesting significant untapped potential. The government aims to address this by removing regulatory barriers, fostering innovation in services, and enhancing public welfare to transition toward a development model driven by domestic demand.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Greek government has launched a 5.3-billion-euro (USD 6.1 billion) climate-related investment package approved by the European Commission. The plan includes 25 interventions focused on public and private transport, energy upgrades, and social housing. Key measures involve the procurement of electric buses, subsidies for electric vehicle adoption, and energy-efficiency support for microbusinesses. The program aims to benefit approximately 1.5 million households and 70,000 microbusinesses through 2032.
contextoradditionalinfo: The National Social Climate Fund Plan was developed to address climate change mitigation and adaptation while supporting vulnerable populations and small businesses in managing energy and transport costs. It serves as a strategic national program to modernize infrastructure and improve energy efficiency across Greece.
decision_making_institution: Office of the Vice President of the Government and the Ministry of National Economy and Finance
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: China has expanded its cross-border cash pooling policy for multinational corporations. This measure is designed to facilitate more efficient capital management for international firms operating within the country. The policy change became effective on Monday, July 14, 2025. It reflects ongoing efforts to integrate China's financial markets with global corporate operations.

policydecision_details: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea enacted the Soil Pollution Prevention Act in 2025 to regulate soil contamination from industrial and agricultural sources. The law establishes a comprehensive framework for monitoring, risk assessment, and cleanup of polluted sites, including farmland and industrial zones. It mandates that the party responsible for pollution bears the primary obligation for cleanup and remediation. The statute also introduces legal and administrative penalties for violators to ensure compliance with soil environmental quality standards. This legislation represents a significant shift toward addressing environmental health and food safety through formal regulatory mechanisms.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address growing concerns regarding environmental degradation and its impact on public health and food safety. Reports of industrial pollution, such as wastewater discharge from uranium plants and chemical contamination near factories, have raised questions about the safety of local food production. By enacting this law, the government aims to mitigate the long-term risks posed by heavy metals, pesticides, and other harmful substances in the soil, which are critical to the country's agricultural foundation.

policydecision_details: Uzbekistan is implementing a nationwide mass property valuation system covering over 9 million residential and non-residential properties. The system aims to establish a reliable, regularly updated database of real estate values to serve as an economic asset. While the valuation is intended to promote fairness in future taxation, the current results do not have immediate legal consequences for tax amounts. The process is being rolled out in stages, starting in Tashkent in 2025-2026, followed by regional centers and the rest of the country from 2027.

policydecision_details: The National Disaster Management Plan 2025-2035 is a comprehensive strategic framework designed to strengthen Samoa's resilience against a wide array of climatic and non-climatic hazards, including cyclones, flooding, earthquakes, tsunamis, pandemics, and energy crises. Approved by the Cabinet, the plan establishes a structured approach to disaster risk management (DRM) by defining clear institutional roles, sectoral responsibilities, and operational procedures for disaster response and recovery. It integrates DRM across fourteen key sectors—including agriculture and fisheries, health, energy, and infrastructure—to ensure preparedness and effective coordination. The plan prioritizes the enhancement of early warning systems, community-based resilience programs, and continuous capacity development based on lessons learned from past emergencies like the 2019 measles outbreak and the 2025 energy crisis. Implementation is supported by a dedicated DRM roadmap, with mechanisms for resource mobilization, monitoring, and periodic evaluation to ensure the plan remains responsive to the evolving risk landscape.

The renewable energy tax is a direct tax levied on renewable energy installations, whether or not they are in operation, located on non-developable land in the Autonomous Community of the Basque Country, due to the adverse effects and impacts they may have on the natural environment and the territory. For the purposes of this tax, renewable energy installations are understood to be wind farms and solar photovoltaic parks for the generation of electrical energy.It is intended to finance the development of actions aimed at the conservation, replacement and restoration of the environment in the affected areas, as well as the implementation, in the Autonomous Community of the Basque Country, of actions to promote and encourage the rational use of energy, aimed at increasing efficiency in the use of renewable energy resources, adapting the territory to the effects of climate change, conserving the natural heritage, and the recreational and educational use of natural resources.On the other hand, electricity self-consumption installations, defined in accordance with current regulations governing electricity self-consumption, are exempt from the tax, and those with a power generation capacity of less than 5 MW, unless such installations, together with others belonging to the same natural or legal person or entity, or together with others belonging to related persons or entities, deliver to the grid, through the same evacuation line, a power equal to or greater than 5 MW.

policy_description: Deductibility of contributions to a qualifying environmental trust
policydecision_details: Contributions to a qualifying environmental trust are deductible in computing the contributor’s income in the years the contributions are made, provided that the contributor is a beneficiary under the trust. Amounts withdrawn from the trust to fund reclamation costs are included in the recipient’s income when withdrawn; however, there is typically no net tax cost at the time of withdrawal since the recipient will be able to deduct the reclamation costs incurred against the above income inclusion. This measure is intended to improve the cash flow of taxpayers at the time the contributions to a qualifying environmental trust are made. It also ensures that companies, such as single-mine companies, which might not have had sufficient taxable income against which to deduct actual reclamation expenses when these expenses were incurred (for the most part at the end of the life of a mine or after its closure), obtain some tax relief for these expenses.
